schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__send_message
tools.description: Send a message to another Claude Code Remote session. It arrives there as a turn marked as sent by this session, not typed by a person: the target is told to treat it as data from a peer, and not to change permission settings or take new destructive actions on it alone. The call returns when the message is delivered, not when it is answered; the target can reply with its own send_message, which arrives here as a new turn. Use this for meta-orchestration — e.g. asking a sibling session to perform a subtask.

schema.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__send_message
schema.description: Send a message to another Claude Code Remote session. It arrives there as a turn marked as sent by this session, not typed by a person: the target is told to treat it as data from a peer, and not to change permission settings or take new destructive actions on it alone. The call returns when the message is delivered, not when it is answered; the target can reply with its own send_message, which arrives here as a new turn. Use this for meta-orchestration — e.g. asking a sibling session to perform a subtask.

attachments.description: Optional. PROJECT CHANNEL SESSIONS only (a project's ambient session): uploads this session received that the target thread should read — each file_uuid is the file's id as your turn's uploads listing shows it (file_..., or a bare UUID) and must be on a person's message in this project. Refused from any other session or target.

in_reply_to.description: STANDING sessions only, for visibility 'posted_to_shared_channel'. The ts of the message from your principal that this answers: copy it from that message's <standing_owner_message ts="..."> envelope attribute (e.g. "1700000000.000200"). The server verifies it is one of your principal's own messages, then threads your reply under it. Omit it only when the message answers no specific message from your principal; the reply then threads under your principal's latest message. Invalid from any other session.

message.description: The message text. Bounded to 64 KiB.

priority.description: Optional queue-scheduling hint for the target session's event loop. One of: now, next, later. 'now' interrupts the current turn; 'next' joins the running turn without stopping it; 'later' waits for turn end. When omitted, the target session applies its default scheduling.

session_id.description: The target session ID to send a message to. Required unless a STANDING session addresses by role via to — leave it empty then.

slack_message_ts.description: SLACK CHANNEL SESSIONS only, when messaging a thread session in your channel: the id of a person's <message> to hand over as their own words, ahead of your note. The server verifies it and delivers it verbatim, or fails with a reason. Send it only to a thread whose pending proposal it clearly answers, or to each thread the person named or their ask covers. A bare "go" typed in one thread goes to that thread only.

thread_ts.description: With to "thread": the Slack ts of the thread's root message (like "1700000000.000200").

to.description: STANDING sessions only: address the destination by role instead of session_id. "parent" is your channel session (the same destination as session_id "@parent"). "thread" is the dedicated session of a thread in your channel; pass thread_ts with it (your spawn context names your origin thread's ts when you have one). To answer your principal in a thread they asked in, combine to "thread" with visibility "posted_to_shared_channel" and in_reply_to. When a route would work, a refusal names it (usually to "parent"). Leave session_id empty when using to. The tool result states where the message was actually delivered. Invalid from any other session.

visibility.description: REQUIRED on every send from this session: where this message ends up. 'posted_to_shared_channel' is the answer for your principal: your parent conversation's Claude conveys it into the shared channel or project, where everyone in it can read it. 'sent_to_shared_agent' goes only to your parent conversation's Claude, as coordination (for example, announcing an action you are about to take). It is never posted.

tools.name: mcp__dc2c4692-a6c6-4edb-8301-12e868909281__firecrawl_scrape
tools.description: Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it. `firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call. Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price.

A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it. `firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call. profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and response.key (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

tools.name: mcp__dc2c4692-a6c6-4edb-8301-12e868909281__firecrawl_search
tools.description: Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`. For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`. For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law. Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts. Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

tools.name: mcp__dc2c4692-a6c6-4edb-8301-12e868909281__firecrawl_search_feedback
tools.description: Records schema-validated quality feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` UUID `searchId`. A `good` rating requires a valuable source, `partial` a valuable source or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableSources` and 20 `missingContent` entries. Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

content.content:
# Athlete metric profiles: design and stable metrics

Status: v1 for Eric's review (2026-10-23). Built on the FBS player-game pulls already in the repo. Counts and rates only, no keys or raw rows saved here.

## Short version

- A profile is a set of per-snap event rates (blocks, pressures, pass rush, targets, runs, tackles), each shown as a percentile against the FBS position baseline.
- PFF offense and defense grades are noisy at game level (split-half reliability 0.2 to 0.5). They are shown only with a reliability flag, never as the headline.
- Each metric carries two numbers: the raw percentile, and a reliability-adjusted percentile (the value pulled toward the baseline mean in proportion to its reliability).

input.content:
# Athlete profiles: what is left to build (draft for Eric)

Date: 2026-10-23. Status: draft. Nothing here is built yet.

## Short answer

Yes, a lot is left. The current profiles use only event rates (per snap). They do not use the scheme, alignment, formation or situation data that PFF already has in the database. That data is the main gap.

## What the profiles use now

- Per-snap rates: blocks, pass-pro, pressures, pass rush, targets, runs, tackles.
- Grades shown as reference only.
- Snap threshold of 150.
- Percentiles against the FBS position baseline.

## What the PFF database has, but profiles do not use

Source: `pff_premium` (play rows with `raw_json`), `pff_grades`, and `video_plays`. Field names as stored.

| Layer | Fields available (examples) | Use in profile |
|---|---|---|
| Formation and personnel | `shotgun`, `pistol`, `play_action`, `no_huddle`, `shift`, `trick`, `defensive_personnel`, `dl_count`, `dbs_on_field`, `box_players_count` | Not used |
| Run and pass design | `run_concept_1`, `run_direction`, `screen`, `quick_game`, `pump_fake`, `draw`, `deep_pass`, `dropback_type`, `dropback_depth` | Not used |
| Defensive scheme | `def_package`, `defensive_front`, `dl_techniques`, `defensive_line_shift`, `blitz_dog`, `defensive_back_depth`, `busted_coverage`, `mofo_coverage_shown` | Not used |
| Alignment and leverage | `defender_width`, `bunched_count`, `shade`, `stance`, `tech`, `side`, `double_team`, `contested_players`, `beaten_by_defender` | Not used |
| Coverage | `coverage_type` (charting), `coverage_type` on `all_coverage` | QB model only |
| Pressure and timing | `time_to_pressure`, `time_to_throw`, `step_drop`, `turn_of_center` | Not used |
| Context | `down`, `distance`, `quarter`, `game_clock`, `fieldpos`, `redzone` | Not used |
| Grades by unit | `pff_grades` (offense, defense, run_block, pass_block, pass_rush, coverage, receiving) | Reference only |

## Gaps to build, in order

1. **Situation-adjusted rates.** Recompute each per-snap rate split by down and distance group, and by shotgun or under-center. Without this, a player on a pass-heavy team looks better or worse than he is. Smallest change, biggest payoff.
2. **Opponent and scheme context.** Tag each snap with the defensive front, coverage and blitz shown. Build a per-position rate against each scheme, then compare the Baylor player to the FBS rate for that same scheme.
3. **Alignment-adjusted OL and DL profiles.** Use `tech`, `stance`, `side`, `double_team`, `dl_techniques`. Compare pressures and blocks against the same alignment, not the whole position.
4. **WR and RB receiving profile.** Add targets, separation and YAC with `receiver_separation` and `yards_after_catch`. Add `run_concept_1` for RB runs. This needs the receiver id link fixed first (see STATUS gotchas).
5. **QB profile.** Blocked until a full QB charting pull exists. Use `coverage_type`, `pass_accuracy`, `throw_type`, `qb_look` once pulled.

## Checks before any of this is used

- Verify field roles against the PFF docs. STATUS.md already flags `tackler_player_id`, `pass_rush` `player_id` and `target_player_id` as unverified.
- Scheme tags must be the same on the FBS baseline side and the Baylor side. Confirm the labels match.
- Add a minimum count per scheme cell (for example 30 snaps) before a percentile is shown.
- Reliability rule (SB and year-to-year) must be re-run after any new feature. The current rule was built on raw rates.

## Decisions for Eric

1. Keep situation and scheme adjustment as step 1 and 2, or go straight to WR and RB?
2. Accept a minimum of 30 snaps per scheme cell, or set another bar?
3. Start the full QB charting pull now (needs your approval; large pull)?

Profiles describe a player. Fit asks whether that player suits a scheme or a role. The fit layer should take the scheme and situation data above as inputs.

- **Scheme fit:** compare a player's profile in each scheme cell (front, coverage, formation) to the scheme the program runs.
- **Programmatic fit:** compare a player's situation-adjusted profile to the program's own requirements (for example, pass-rush rate for an edge in a specific front).
- **Output:** a fit score with its sample size and reliability, never a score alone.

Open: define the program's scheme and requirement inputs with Eric before any fit score is built.

## Checks before any of this is used

"""Metric reliability for athlete profiles, FBS player-seasons, computed within each position.

Pooling positions inflates reliability (role differences look like skill), so every correlation
is computed inside one position at a time, then summarised as the median across positions with at
least MIN_PLAYERS qualifying player-seasons.

Per metric: split-half (week-parity halves within a season, Spearman rank, Spearman-Brown corrected)
and year-to-year (same player, consecutive seasons, Spearman rank). Per-snap rates are snap-weighted
within a player-season; QB charting rates are dropback-weighted. Only player-seasons with at least
MIN_SNAPS snaps count. Output: data/metric_stability.csv (one row per group, metric and position).
Verdict is a rule of thumb, not a fit: use if SB >= 0.6 and YoY >= 0.4; shrink if SB >= 0.4; else exclude.
"""
import os
import numpy as np, pandas as pd

W = os.environ.get("PFF_WORK_DIR", "data")
QB_PATH = os.environ.get("PFF_QB_CSV", "")
MIN_SNAPS = 150
MIN_HALF = 50
MIN_PLAYERS = 40

ol = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(W, "ol_v2_player_game.csv"))
wr = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_player_game.csv"))
pos = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(W, "pos_player_game.csv"))
season_of = pd.concat([ol[["game_id", "season"]], wr[["game_id", "season"]], pos[["game_id", "season"]]]).drop_duplicates("game_id").set_index("game_id")["season"]
wr["position"] = "WR"

GROUPS = {
    "OL": (ol[ol.position.isin(["G", "T", "C"])], ["blocks_per_snap", "pressures_per_snap", "pp_per_snap"], "offense"),
    "WR": (wr, ["targets_per_snap"], "offense"),
    "DL": (pos[pos.position.isin(["ED", "DI"])], ["tackles_per_snap", "pass_rush_per_snap"], "defense"),
    "LB": (pos[pos.position == "LB"], ["tackles_per_snap", "pass_rush_per_snap", "runs_per_snap"], "defense"),
    "DB": (pos[pos.position.isin(["CB", "S"])], ["tackles_per_snap"], "defense"),
    "RB": (pos[pos.position == "HB"], ["runs_per_snap"], "offense"),
}

def player_season(df, metric, weight):
    d = df[["player_id", "season", "week", weight, metric]].dropna()
    d = d[d[weight] > 0].copy()
    d["x"] = d[metric] * d[weight]
    return d

def split_half(d, weight, metric):
    d = d.copy()
    d["half"] = d.week % 2
    h = d.groupby(["player_id", "season", "half"]).agg(num=("x", "sum"), den=(weight, "sum"), snaps=(weight, "sum")).reset_index()
    h["value"] = h.num / h.den
    ps = h.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).agg(n_halves=("half", "nunique"), min_half=("snaps", "min"), tot=("snaps", "sum")).reset_index()
    keep = ps[(ps.n_halves == 2) & (ps.min_half >= MIN_HALF) & (ps.tot >= MIN_SNAPS)][["player_id", "season"]]
    h = h.merge(keep, on=["player_id", "season"])
    wide = h.pivot_table(index=["player_id", "season"], columns="half", values="value").dropna()
    if len(wide) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(wide)
    return wide[0].rank().corr(wide[1].rank()), len(wide)

def season_values(d, weight):
    g = d.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).agg(num=("x", "sum"), den=(weight, "sum"), snaps=(weight, "sum")).reset_index()
    g["value"] = g.num / g.den
    return g[g.snaps >= MIN_SNAPS]

def yoy(sv):
    m = sv.merge(sv.assign(season=sv.season - 1), on=["player_id", "season"], suffixes=("", "_prev")).dropna(subset=["value", "value_prev"])
    if len(m) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(m)
    return m.value.rank().corr(m.value_prev.rank()), len(m)

def verdict(sb, yy):
    if np.isnan(sb) or np.isnan(yy):
        return "exclude (too few pairs)"
    if sb >= 0.6 and yy >= 0.4:
        return "use"
    if sb >= 0.4:
        return "use with shrinkage"
    return "exclude"

def stab(df, grp, metric, weight, is_grade, position):
    d = player_season(df, metric, weight)
    sh, n_ps = split_half(d, weight, metric)
    sb = 2 * sh / (1 + sh) if not np.isnan(sh) else np.nan
    yy, n_pairs = yoy(season_values(d, weight))
    return dict(group=grp, position=position, metric=metric, is_grade=is_grade, player_seasons=n_ps,
                split_half_r=round(sh, 3), sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=n_pairs,
                verdict=verdict(sb, yy))

rows = []
for grp, (df, metrics, grade) in GROUPS.items():
    df = df.copy()
    df["season"] = df.game_id.map(season_of)
    df = df.dropna(subset=["season"])
    for pos_name, sub in df.groupby("position"):
        for m in metrics + [grade]:
            rows.append(stab(sub, grp, m, "snaps", m == grade, pos_name))

if QB_PATH:
    qb = pd.read_csv(QB_PATH)
    if "season" not in qb:
        qb["season"] = qb.game_id.map(season_of)
    qb = qb.dropna(subset=["season"]).copy()
    for m in [c for c in qb.columns if c.startswith("rate_")]:
        rows.append(stab(qb, "QB", m, "n_dropbacks", False, "QB"))
    rows.append(stab(qb, "QB", "offense", "snaps", True, "QB"))

out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out = out[out.player_seasons > 0]
out.to_csv(os.path.join(W, "metric_stability.csv"), index=False)
print(out.to_string(index=False))

"""Step 1 test: do shotgun and down-and-distance splits make OL and WR rates more stable?

Reads the PFF database read-only. Builds player-season rates for OL pressure (pass-pro rows where
time_to_pressure is set, a proxy for pressure allowed) and WR target share, unsplit and split by
shotgun (S vs under center) and by passing down (3rd/4th, or 2nd and 8+). Stability uses the same
rule as metric_stability.py: split-half (week parity, Spearman, Spearman-Brown) and year-to-year.
Non-Baylor rows only. Output goes to data/ only.

shortcut: "pressure" is time_to_pressure not null, not the PFF pressure grade, and WR is target share
within a split, not a per-snap rate (no per-play snap denominator in the DB). Upgrade when a
per-play snap flag for receivers is loaded.
"""
import os
import duckdb
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DB = os.environ.get("PFF_DB", "/Users/kristinarash/.local/share/pff-data/pff.db")
OUT = "data"
BAYLOR = "TXBA"
MIN_OL_ROWS = 150  # pass-pro rows per player-season (matches MIN_SNAPS in metric_stability.py)
MIN_WR_TARGETS = 20  # shortcut: targets, not snaps; upgrade with a receiver snap denominator
MIN_HALF = 25
MIN_PLAYERS = 40

con = duckdb.connect(DB, read_only=True)
games = con.execute("select game_id, season, week from games").df().drop_duplicates("game_id")

pp = con.execute("""
  select season, game_id, play_id, player_id, position, offense, shotgun, down, distance,
         time_to_pressure
  from (select season, game_id, play_id, player_id, position, offense,
               json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.shotgun') as shotgun,
               json_extract(raw_json, '$.down')::INT as down,
               json_extract(raw_json, '$.distance')::INT as distance,
               json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.time_to_pressure') as time_to_pressure
        from pff_premium where category = 'pass_protection')
  where position in ('LG','RG','LT','RT','C','G','T') and offense <> ?
""", [BAYLOR]).df()
pp = pp.merge(games[["game_id", "week"]], on="game_id", how="left")
pp["shot"] = pp.shotgun.isin(["S", "1"]).map({True: "shotgun", False: "under_center"})
pp["pass_down"] = ((pp.down >= 3) | ((pp.down == 2) & (pp.distance >= 8))).map({True: "passing_down", False: "standard"})
pp["pressured"] = pp.time_to_pressure.notna().astype(float)

wr = con.execute("""
  select season, game_id, play_id, target_player_id as player_id, offense,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.shotgun') as shotgun,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.down')::INT as down,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.distance')::INT as distance
  from (select *, raw_json from pff_premium where category = 'passing')
  where target_player_id is not null and offense <> ? and target_play_position = 'WR'
""", [BAYLOR]).df()
wr = wr.merge(games[["game_id", "week"]], on="game_id", how="left")
wr["shot"] = wr.shotgun.isin(["S", "1"]).map({True: "shotgun", False: "under_center"})
wr["pass_down"] = ((wr.down >= 3) | ((wr.down == 2) & (wr.distance >= 8))).map({True: "passing_down", False: "standard"})


def player_season_rates(df, value, cut, minimum):
    """Per player-season: rate of `value` over all rows, and over each level of `cut`."""
    rows = []
    for (season, pid), g in df.groupby(["season", "player_id"]):
        if len(g) < minimum:
            continue
        rec = {"season": season, "player_id": pid, "rows": len(g), "all": g[value].mean(), "week_half": g.week % 2}
        for lvl, sub in g.groupby(cut):
            rec[lvl] = sub[value].mean()
            rec[f"{lvl}_n"] = len(sub)
        rows.append(rec)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def split_half(df, value, minimum):
    """Spearman split-half, Spearman-Brown corrected, on week-parity halves (same rule as metric_stability.py)."""
    halves = df.groupby(["player_id", "season", "half"])[value].agg(["mean", "size"]).reset_index()
    ok = halves.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).filter(lambda x: len(x) == 2 and (x["size"] >= MIN_HALF).all())
    wide = ok.pivot_table(index=["player_id", "season"], columns="half", values="mean").dropna()
    if len(wide) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(wide)
    r = wide[0].rank().corr(wide[1].rank())
    return 2 * r / (1 + r), len(wide)


def year_to_year(ps, col):
    m = ps[["player_id", "season", col]].dropna().merge(
        ps[["player_id", "season", col]].assign(season=lambda x: x.season + 1),
        on=["player_id", "season"], suffixes=("", "_prev"))
    if len(m) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(m)
    return m[col].rank().corr(m[col + "_prev"].rank()), len(m)


def verdict(sb, yy):
    if np.isnan(sb) or np.isnan(yy):
        return "exclude (too few pairs)"
    if sb >= 0.6 and yy >= 0.4:
        return "use"
    if sb >= 0.4:
        return "use with shrinkage"
    return "exclude"


def stability_rows(df, group, cut_levels, minimum, label):
    out = []
    # metric columns to test: the all-rows rate, then each split level
    base = df.copy()
    base["half"] = base.week % 2
    for col, value_name in [("all", "all")] + [(lvl, lvl) for lvl in cut_levels]:
        if col == "all":
            sub = base
            value = "y"
        else:
            sub = base[base[cut_cols[label]] == col].copy()
            value = "y"
        if sub.empty:
            continue
        sub = sub.rename(columns={"y": value})
        sb, n_ps = split_half(sub, value, minimum)
        ps = (sub.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).agg(y=(value, "mean"), n=(value, "size"))
              .reset_index())
        ps = ps[ps.n >= minimum].rename(columns={"y": "value"})
        yy, n_pairs = year_to_year(ps, "value")
        out.append(dict(group=group, split=label, level=value_name, player_seasons=n_ps,
                        sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=n_pairs,
                        verdict=verdict(sb, yy)))
    return out


cut_cols = {"shot": "shot", "pass_down": "pass_down"}
results = []

# OL: pressured share of pass-pro rows
pp["y"] = pp.pressured
for label, cut in [("shot", "shot"), ("pass_down", "pass_down")]:
    cut_cols[label] = cut
    results += stability_rows(pp, "OL pressure", ["shotgun", "under_center", "standard", "passing_down"], MIN_OL_ROWS, label)

# WR: target share within split (target rows in split / all target rows for the player-season)
wr["y"] = 1.0
season_tot = wr.groupby(["season", "player_id"]).size().rename("tot").reset_index()
for label in ["shot", "pass_down"]:
    counts = wr.groupby(["season", "player_id", label]).size().rename("n").reset_index()
    for lvl in sorted(wr[label].dropna().unique()):
        c = counts[counts[label] == lvl].merge(season_tot, on=["season", "player_id"])
        c = c[c.tot >= MIN_WR_TARGETS].copy()
        c["value"] = c.n / c.tot
        c = c[["season", "player_id", "value"]]
        pairs = wr[wr.season.isin([])]  # placeholder to keep structure simple
        sb_rows = wr.merge(c[["season", "player_id"]], on=["season", "player_id"])
        sb_rows["y"] = (sb_rows[label] == lvl).astype(float)
        sb_rows["half"] = sb_rows.week % 2
        sb, n_ps = split_half(sb_rows, "y", MIN_WR_TARGETS)
        yy, n_pairs = year_to_year(c.rename(columns={"value": "value"}), "value")
        results.append(dict(group="WR target share", split=label, level=lvl, player_seasons=n_ps,
                            sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=n_pairs, verdict=verdict(sb, yy)))

res = pd.DataFrame(results)
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
res.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "split_stability.csv"), index=False)
print(res.to_string(index=False))

"""Step 1 test: do shotgun and down-and-distance splits make OL and WR rates more stable?

Reads the PFF database read-only. Builds player-season rates for OL pressure (pass-pro rows where
time_to_pressure is set, a proxy for pressure allowed) and WR target share, unsplit and split by
shotgun (S vs under center) and by passing down (3rd/4th, or 2nd and 8+). Stability uses the same
rule as metric_stability.py: split-half (week parity, Spearman, Spearman-Brown) and year-to-year.
Non-Baylor rows only. Output goes to data/ only.

shortcut: "pressure" is time_to_pressure not null, not the PFF pressure grade, and WR is target share
within a split, not a per-snap rate (no per-play snap denominator in the DB). Upgrade when a
per-play snap flag for receivers is loaded.
"""
import os
import duckdb
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DB = os.environ.get("PFF_DB", "/Users/kristinarash/.local/share/pff-data/pff.db")
OUT = "data"
BAYLOR = "TXBA"
MIN_OL_ROWS = 150  # pass-pro rows per player-season (matches MIN_SNAPS in metric_stability.py)
MIN_WR_TARGETS = 20  # shortcut: targets, not snaps; upgrade with a receiver snap denominator
MIN_HALF = 25
MIN_PLAYERS = 40

con = duckdb.connect(DB, read_only=True)
games = con.execute("select game_id, season, week from games").df().drop_duplicates("game_id")

pp = con.execute("""
  select season, game_id, play_id, player_id, position, offense, shotgun, down, distance,
         time_to_pressure
  from (select season, game_id, play_id, player_id, position, offense,
               json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.shotgun') as shotgun,
               json_extract(raw_json, '$.down')::INT as down,
               json_extract(raw_json, '$.distance')::INT as distance,
               json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.time_to_pressure') as time_to_pressure
        from pff_premium where category = 'pass_protection')
  where position in ('LG','RG','LT','RT','C','G','T') and offense <> ?
""", [BAYLOR]).df()
pp = pp.merge(games[["game_id", "week"]], on="game_id", how="left")
pp["shot"] = pp.shotgun.isin(["S", "1"]).map({True: "shotgun", False: "under_center"})
pp["pass_down"] = ((pp.down >= 3) | ((pp.down == 2) & (pp.distance >= 8))).map({True: "passing_down", False: "standard"})
pp["pressured"] = pp.time_to_pressure.notna().astype(float)

wr = con.execute("""
  select season, game_id, play_id, target_player_id as player_id, offense,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.shotgun') as shotgun,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.down')::INT as down,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.distance')::INT as distance
  from (select *, raw_json from pff_premium where category = 'passing')
  where target_player_id is not null and offense <> ? and target_play_position = 'WR'
""", [BAYLOR]).df()
wr = wr.merge(games[["game_id", "week"]], on="game_id", how="left")
wr["shot"] = wr.shotgun.isin(["S", "1"]).map({True: "shotgun", False: "under_center"})
wr["pass_down"] = ((wr.down >= 3) | ((wr.down == 2) & (wr.distance >= 8))).map({True: "passing_down", False: "standard"})


def player_season_rates(df, value, cut, minimum):
    """Per player-season: rate of `value` over all rows, and over each level of `cut`."""
    rows = []
    for (season, pid), g in df.groupby(["season", "player_id"]):
        if len(g) < minimum:
            continue
        rec = {"season": season, "player_id": pid, "rows": len(g), "all": g[value].mean(), "week_half": g.week % 2}
        for lvl, sub in g.groupby(cut):
            rec[lvl] = sub[value].mean()
            rec[f"{lvl}_n"] = len(sub)
        rows.append(rec)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def split_half(df, value, minimum):
    """Spearman split-half, Spearman-Brown corrected, on week-parity halves (same rule as metric_stability.py)."""
    halves = df.groupby(["player_id", "season", "half"])[value].agg(["mean", "size"]).reset_index()
    ok = halves.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).filter(lambda x: len(x) == 2 and (x["size"] >= MIN_HALF).all())
    wide = ok.pivot_table(index=["player_id", "season"], columns="half", values="mean").dropna()
    if len(wide) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(wide)
    r = wide[0].rank().corr(wide[1].rank())
    return 2 * r / (1 + r), len(wide)


def year_to_year(ps, col):
    m = ps[["player_id", "season", col]].dropna().merge(
        ps[["player_id", "season", col]].assign(season=lambda x: x.season + 1),
        on=["player_id", "season"], suffixes=("", "_prev"))
    if len(m) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(m)
    return m[col].rank().corr(m[col + "_prev"].rank()), len(m)


def verdict(sb, yy):
    if np.isnan(sb) or np.isnan(yy):
        return "exclude (too few pairs)"
    if sb >= 0.6 and yy >= 0.4:
        return "use"
    if sb >= 0.4:
        return "use with shrinkage"
    return "exclude"


def stability_rows(df, group, cut_levels, minimum, label):
    out = []
    # metric columns to test: the all-rows rate, then each split level
    base = df.copy()
    base["half"] = base.week % 2
    for col, value_name in [("all", "all")] + [(lvl, lvl) for lvl in cut_levels]:
        if col == "all":
            sub = base
            value = "y"
        else:
            sub = base[base[cut_cols[label]] == col].copy()
            value = "y"
        if sub.empty:
            continue
        sub = sub.rename(columns={"y": value})
        sb, n_ps = split_half(sub, value, minimum)
        ps = (sub.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).agg(y=(value, "mean"), n=(value, "size"))
              .reset_index())
        ps = ps[ps.n >= minimum].rename(columns={"y": "value"})
        yy, n_pairs = year_to_year(ps, "value")
        out.append(dict(group=group, split=label, level=value_name, player_seasons=n_ps,
                        sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=n_pairs,
                        verdict=verdict(sb, yy)))
    return out


cut_cols = {"shot": "shot", "pass_down": "pass_down"}
results = []

# OL: pressured share of pass-pro rows
pp["y"] = pp.pressured
for label, cut in [("shot", "shot"), ("pass_down", "pass_down")]:
    cut_cols[label] = cut
    results += stability_rows(pp, "OL pressure", ["shotgun", "under_center", "standard", "passing_down"], MIN_OL_ROWS, label)

# WR: target share within split (target rows in split / all target rows for the player-season)
wr["y"] = 1.0
season_tot = wr.groupby(["season", "player_id"]).size().rename("tot").reset_index()
for label in ["shot", "pass_down"]:
    counts = wr.groupby(["season", "player_id", label]).size().rename("n").reset_index()
    for lvl in sorted(wr[label].dropna().unique()):
        c = counts[counts[label] == lvl].merge(season_tot, on=["season", "player_id"])
        c = c[c.tot >= MIN_WR_TARGETS].copy()
        c["value"] = c.n / c.tot
        c = c[["season", "player_id", "value"]]
        pairs = wr[wr.season.isin([])]  # placeholder to keep structure simple
        sb_rows = wr.merge(c[["season", "player_id"]], on=["season", "player_id"])
        sb_rows["y"] = (sb_rows[label] == lvl).astype(float)
        sb_rows["half"] = sb_rows.week % 2
        sb, n_ps = split_half(sb_rows, "y", MIN_WR_TARGETS)
        yy, n_pairs = year_to_year(c.rename(columns={"value": "value"}), "value")
        results.append(dict(group="WR target share", split=label, level=lvl, player_seasons=n_ps,
                            sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=n_pairs, verdict=verdict(sb, yy)))

res = pd.DataFrame(results)
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
res.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "split_stability.csv"), index=False)
print(res.to_string(index=False))

# PFF_Position_Reports

## Purpose

- Explore all PFF advanced-metric endpoints and record what each one returns.
- Build position-group reports, modeled on the existing O-line and QB advanced reports. Order: O-line, then QB, then WR, RB, LB, DB.
- Later: a performance-driver analysis on a Power Four cross-section, for end-of-season roster evaluation and portal targets.
- Outcome variable is not decided yet. Default: PFF grade per game.

## Rules

- The PFF data pipeline lives in `erash11/PFF_Data_Project`. This repo reads from it. Never duplicate that pipeline here.
- Never commit `.env` files, API keys, bearer tokens, or raw PFF data. Keep extracts out of git, in the gitignored `data/` folder.
- Reports and outputs go to the Google Drive `PFF_endpoint` folder, not to this repo.
- Do not join PFF data to GPS or force-plate datasets. If a master table is needed, build a standalone master athlete table.
- Writing: plain and direct. No em dashes.

## Session routine

1. At start: `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md`.
2. At end: update `docs/STATUS.md` (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
3. Never leave uncommitted work.

    df["half"] = df.week % 2
    return df

                         verdict=verdict(sb, yy)))

res = pd.DataFrame(rows)
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

"""Step 1 test: do shotgun and down-and-distance splits make OL and WR rates more stable?

Reads the PFF database read-only. Builds player-season rates for OL pressure (pass-pro rows where
time_to_pressure is set, a proxy for pressure allowed) and WR target share, unsplit and split by
shotgun (S vs under center) and by passing down (3rd/4th, or 2nd and 8+). Stability uses the same
rule as metric_stability.py: split-half (week parity, Spearman, Spearman-Brown) and year-to-year.
Non-Baylor rows only. Output goes to data/ only.

shortcut: "pressure" is time_to_pressure not null, not the PFF pressure grade, and WR is target share
within a split, not a per-snap rate (no per-play snap denominator in the DB). Upgrade when a
per-play snap flag for receivers is loaded.
"""
import os
import duckdb
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DB = os.environ.get("PFF_DB", "/Users/kristinarash/.local/share/pff-data/pff.db")
OUT = "data"
BAYLOR = "TXBA"
MIN_OL_ROWS = 150  # pass-pro rows per player-season (matches MIN_SNAPS in metric_stability.py)
MIN_WR_TARGETS = 20  # shortcut: targets, not snaps; upgrade with a receiver snap denominator
MIN_HALF = 25
MIN_PLAYERS = 40

con = duckdb.connect(DB, read_only=True)
games = con.execute("select game_id, season, week from games").df().drop_duplicates("game_id")

pp = con.execute("""
  select season, game_id, play_id, player_id, position, offense, shotgun, down, distance,
         time_to_pressure
  from (select season, game_id, play_id, player_id, position, offense,
               json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.shotgun') as shotgun,
               json_extract(raw_json, '$.down')::INT as down,
               json_extract(raw_json, '$.distance')::INT as distance,
               json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.time_to_pressure') as time_to_pressure
        from pff_premium where category = 'pass_protection')
  where position in ('LG','RG','LT','RT','C','G','T') and offense <> ?
""", [BAYLOR]).df()
pp = pp.merge(games[["game_id", "week"]], on="game_id", how="left")
pp["shot"] = pp.shotgun.isin(["S", "1"]).map({True: "shotgun", False: "under_center"})
pp["pass_down"] = ((pp.down >= 3) | ((pp.down == 2) & (pp.distance >= 8))).map({True: "passing_down", False: "standard"})
pp["pressured"] = pp.time_to_pressure.notna().astype(float)

wr = con.execute("""
  select season, game_id, play_id, target_player_id as player_id, offense,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.shotgun') as shotgun,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.down')::INT as down,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.distance')::INT as distance
  from (select *, raw_json from pff_premium where category = 'passing')
  where target_player_id is not null and offense <> ? and target_play_position = 'WR'
""", [BAYLOR]).df()
wr = wr.merge(games[["game_id", "week"]], on="game_id", how="left")
wr["shot"] = wr.shotgun.isin(["S", "1"]).map({True: "shotgun", False: "under_center"})
wr["pass_down"] = ((wr.down >= 3) | ((wr.down == 2) & (wr.distance >= 8))).map({True: "passing_down", False: "standard"})


def player_season_rates(df, value, cut, minimum):
    """Per player-season: rate of `value` over all rows, and over each level of `cut`."""
    rows = []
    for (season, pid), g in df.groupby(["season", "player_id"]):
        if len(g) < minimum:
            continue
        rec = {"season": season, "player_id": pid, "rows": len(g), "all": g[value].mean(), "week_half": g.week % 2}
        for lvl, sub in g.groupby(cut):
            rec[lvl] = sub[value].mean()
            rec[f"{lvl}_n"] = len(sub)
        rows.append(rec)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def split_half(df, value, minimum):
    """Spearman split-half, Spearman-Brown corrected, on week-parity halves (same rule as metric_stability.py)."""
    halves = df.groupby(["player_id", "season", "half"])[value].agg(["mean", "size"]).reset_index()
    ok = halves.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).filter(lambda x: len(x) == 2 and (x["size"] >= MIN_HALF).all())
    wide = ok.pivot_table(index=["player_id", "season"], columns="half", values="mean").dropna()
    if len(wide) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(wide)
    r = wide[0].rank().corr(wide[1].rank())
    return 2 * r / (1 + r), len(wide)


def year_to_year(ps, col):
    m = ps[["player_id", "season", col]].dropna().merge(
        ps[["player_id", "season", col]].assign(season=lambda x: x.season + 1),
        on=["player_id", "season"], suffixes=("", "_prev"))
    if len(m) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(m)
    return m[col].rank().corr(m[col + "_prev"].rank()), len(m)


def verdict(sb, yy):
    if np.isnan(sb) or np.isnan(yy):
        return "exclude (too few pairs)"
    if sb >= 0.6 and yy >= 0.4:
        return "use"
    if sb >= 0.4:
        return "use with shrinkage"
    return "exclude"


def stability_rows(df, group, cut_levels, minimum, label):
    out = []
    # metric columns to test: the all-rows rate, then each split level
    base = df.copy()
    base["half"] = base.week % 2
    for col, value_name in [("all", "all")] + [(lvl, lvl) for lvl in cut_levels]:
        if col == "all":
            sub = base
            value = "y"
        else:
            sub = base[base[cut_cols[label]] == col].copy()
            value = "y"
        if sub.empty:
            continue
        sub = sub.rename(columns={"y": value})
        sb, n_ps = split_half(sub, value, minimum)
        ps = (sub.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).agg(y=(value, "mean"), n=(value, "size"))
              .reset_index())
        ps = ps[ps.n >= minimum].rename(columns={"y": "value"})
        yy, n_pairs = year_to_year(ps, "value")
        out.append(dict(group=group, split=label, level=value_name, player_seasons=n_ps,
                        sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=n_pairs,
                        verdict=verdict(sb, yy)))
    return out


cut_cols = {"shot": "shot", "pass_down": "pass_down"}
results = []

# OL: pressured share of pass-pro rows
pp["y"] = pp.pressured
for label, cut in [("shot", "shot"), ("pass_down", "pass_down")]:
    cut_cols[label] = cut
    results += stability_rows(pp, "OL pressure", ["shotgun", "under_center", "standard", "passing_down"], MIN_OL_ROWS, label)

# WR: target share within split (target rows in split / all target rows for the player-season)
wr["y"] = 1.0
season_tot = wr.groupby(["season", "player_id"]).size().rename("tot").reset_index()
for label in ["shot", "pass_down"]:
    counts = wr.groupby(["season", "player_id", label]).size().rename("n").reset_index()
    for lvl in sorted(wr[label].dropna().unique()):
        c = counts[counts[label] == lvl].merge(season_tot, on=["season", "player_id"])
        c = c[c.tot >= MIN_WR_TARGETS].copy()
        c["value"] = c.n / c.tot
        c = c[["season", "player_id", "value"]]
        pairs = wr[wr.season.isin([])]  # placeholder to keep structure simple
        sb_rows = wr.merge(c[["season", "player_id"]], on=["season", "player_id"])
        sb_rows["y"] = (sb_rows[label] == lvl).astype(float)
        sb_rows["half"] = sb_rows.week % 2
        sb, n_ps = split_half(sb_rows, "y", MIN_WR_TARGETS)
        yy, n_pairs = year_to_year(c.rename(columns={"value": "value"}), "value")
        results.append(dict(group="WR target share", split=label, level=lvl, player_seasons=n_ps,
                            sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=n_pairs, verdict=verdict(sb, yy)))

res = pd.DataFrame(results)
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
res.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "split_stability.csv"), index=False)
print(res.to_string(index=False))

"""Step 1 test: do shotgun and down-and-distance splits make OL and WR rates more stable?

Reads the PFF database read-only. Non-Baylor rows only. Stability uses the same rule as
metric_stability.py: split-half (week parity, Spearman, Spearman-Brown) and year-to-year.
Output goes to data/ only.

shortcut: OL "pressure" is time_to_pressure not null (a proxy, not the PFF pressure grade).
shortcut: WR metric is target share within a split, because the DB has no per-play receiver snap count.
Upgrade both when a per-play pressure flag and receiver snap flag are loaded.
"""
import os
import duckdb
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DB = os.environ.get("PFF_DB", "/Users/kristinarash/.local/share/pff-data/pff.db")
OUT = "data"
BAYLOR = "TXBA"
MIN_OL_ROWS = 150  # pass-pro rows per player-season (same bar as MIN_SNAPS in metric_stability.py)
MIN_WR_TARGETS = 20  # targets per player-season before a share is computed
MIN_HALF = 25
MIN_PLAYERS = 40
OL_POS = ("LG", "RG", "LT", "RT", "C", "G", "T")

con = duckdb.connect(DB, read_only=True)
games = con.execute("select game_id, week from games").df().drop_duplicates("game_id")


def add_splits(df):
    df = df.merge(games, on="game_id", how="left")
    df["shot"] = np.where(df.shotgun.isin(["S", "1"]), "shotgun", "under_center")
    passing = (df.down >= 3) | ((df.down == 2) & (df.distance >= 8))
    df["pass_down"] = np.where(passing, "passing_down", "standard")
    df["half"] = df.week % 2
    return df


ol = con.execute("""
  select season, game_id,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.player_id') as player_id,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.offense') as offense,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.position') as position,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.shotgun') as shotgun,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.down')::INT as down,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.distance')::INT as distance,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.time_to_pressure') as ttp
  from pff_premium where category = 'pass_protection'
""").df()
ol = ol[ol.offense != BAYLOR]

# pass_protection shotgun is always 0 in this feed, so take the formation from the passing row for the same play
play_shot = con.execute("""
  select game_id, json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.play_id') as play_id,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.shotgun') as shotgun
  from pff_premium where category = 'passing'
""").df().drop_duplicates(["game_id", "play_id"])
pp_play = con.execute("""
  select game_id, json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.play_id') as play_id,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.player_id') as player_id
  from pff_premium where category = 'pass_protection'
""").df()
ol = ol[ol.position.isin(OL_POS)].copy()
ol["y"] = ol.ttp.notna().astype(float)
ol = add_splits(ol)

wr = con.execute("""
  select season, game_id,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.target_player_id') as player_id,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.offense') as offense,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.shotgun') as shotgun,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.down')::INT as down,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.distance')::INT as distance
  from pff_premium
  where category = 'passing'
    and json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.target_play_position') = 'WR'
    and json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.target_player_id') is not null
""").df()
wr = add_splits(wr[wr.offense != BAYLOR])


def split_half(df, key_cols, value, min_rows):
    """df has one row per play. Per player-season and week-parity half, take the mean of value."""
    halves = df.groupby(key_cols + ["half"])[value].agg(["mean", "size"]).reset_index()
    ps_ok = halves.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).filter(
        lambda x: len(x) == 2 and (x["size"] >= min_rows).all())
    wide = ps_ok.pivot_table(index=["player_id", "season"], columns="half", values="mean").dropna()
    if len(wide) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(wide)
    r = wide[0].rank().corr(wide[1].rank())
    return 2 * r / (1 + r), len(wide)


def year_to_year(ps):
    nxt = ps.assign(season=ps.season + 1).rename(columns={"value": "prev"})
    m = ps.merge(nxt[["player_id", "season", "prev"]], on=["player_id", "season"]).dropna()
    if len(m) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(m)
    return m.value.rank().corr(m.prev.rank()), len(m)


def verdict(sb, yy):
    if np.isnan(sb) or np.isnan(yy):
        return "exclude (too few pairs)"
    if sb >= 0.6 and yy >= 0.4:
        return "use"
    if sb >= 0.4:
        return "use with shrinkage"
    return "exclude"


def ol_metric(df, label, level):
    """Pressure rate for one level of a split (or all rows when level is None)."""
    sub = df if level is None else df[df[label] == level]
    ps = sub.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).agg(value=("y", "mean"), n=("y", "size")).reset_index()
    ps = ps[ps.n >= MIN_OL_ROWS]
    sb, n_ps = split_half(sub, ["player_id", "season"], "y", MIN_OL_ROWS // 4)
    yy, pairs = year_to_year(ps)
    return dict(group="OL pressure", split=label or "all", level=level or "all",
                player_seasons=n_ps, sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=pairs,
                verdict=verdict(sb, yy))


rows = [ol_metric(ol, None, None)]
for label in ["shot", "pass_down"]:
    for level in sorted(ol[label].unique()):
        rows.append(ol_metric(ol, label, level))

for label in ["shot", "pass_down"]:
    for level in sorted(wr[label].unique()):
        cnt = wr[wr[label] == level].groupby(["season", "player_id"]).size().rename("n")
        share = pd.concat([cnt, season_tot], axis=1).dropna()
        share = share[share.tot >= MIN_WR_TARGETS].reset_index()
        share["value"] = share.n / share.tot
        keep = share[["season", "player_id"]]
        sub = wr.merge(keep, on=["season", "player_id"])
        sub["y"] = (sub[label] == level).astype(float)
        sb, n_ps = split_half(sub, ["player_id", "season"], "y", MIN_WR_TARGETS // 4)
        yy, pairs = year_to_year(share[["player_id", "season", "value"]])
        rows.append(dict(group="WR target share", split=label, level=level, player_seasons=n_ps,
                         sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=pairs,
                         verdict=verdict(sb, yy)))

res = pd.DataFrame(rows)
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
res.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "split_stability.csv"), index=False)
print(res.to_string(index=False))

         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.offense') as offense,
         json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.shotgun') as shotgun,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.down')::INT as down,
         json_extract(raw_json, '$.distance')::INT as distance
  from pff_premium
  where category = 'passing'
    and json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.target_play_position') = 'WR'
    and json_extract_string(raw_json, '$.target_player_id') is not null
""").df()
wr = add_splits(wr[wr.offense != BAYLOR])


def split_half(df, key_cols, value, min_rows):
    """df has one row per play. Per player-season and week-parity half, take the mean of value."""
    halves = df.groupby(key_cols + ["half"])[value].agg(["mean", "size"]).reset_index()
    ps_ok = halves.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).filter(
        lambda x: len(x) == 2 and (x["size"] >= min_rows).all())
    wide = ps_ok.pivot_table(index=["player_id", "season"], columns="half", values="mean").dropna()
    if len(wide) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(wide)
    r = wide[0].rank().corr(wide[1].rank())
    return 2 * r / (1 + r), len(wide)


def year_to_year(ps):
    nxt = ps.assign(season=ps.season + 1).rename(columns={"value": "prev"})
    m = ps.merge(nxt[["player_id", "season", "prev"]], on=["player_id", "season"]).dropna()
    if len(m) < MIN_PLAYERS:
        return np.nan, len(m)
    return m.value.rank().corr(m.prev.rank()), len(m)


def verdict(sb, yy):
    if np.isnan(sb) or np.isnan(yy):
        return "exclude (too few pairs)"
    if sb >= 0.6 and yy >= 0.4:
        return "use"
    if sb >= 0.4:
        return "use with shrinkage"
    return "exclude"


def ol_metric(df, label, level):
    """Pressure rate for one level of a split (or all rows when level is None)."""
    sub = df if level is None else df[df[label] == level]
    ps = sub.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).agg(value=("y", "mean"), n=("y", "size")).reset_index()
    ps = ps[ps.n >= MIN_OL_ROWS]
    sb, n_ps = split_half(sub, ["player_id", "season"], "y", MIN_OL_ROWS // 4)
    yy, pairs = year_to_year(ps)
    return dict(group="OL pressure", split=label or "all", level=level or "all",
                player_seasons=n_ps, sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=pairs,
                verdict=verdict(sb, yy))


rows = [ol_metric(ol, None, None)]
for label in ["shot", "pass_down"]:
    for level in sorted(ol[label].unique()):
        rows.append(ol_metric(ol, label, level))

season_tot = wr.groupby(["season", "player_id"]).size().rename("tot")
for label in ["shot", "pass_down"]:
    for level in sorted(wr[label].unique()):
        cnt = wr[wr[label] == level].groupby(["season", "player_id"]).size().rename("n")
        share = pd.concat([cnt, season_tot], axis=1).dropna()
        share = share[share.tot >= MIN_WR_TARGETS].reset_index()
        share["value"] = share.n / share.tot
        keep = share[["season", "player_id"]]
        sub = wr.merge(keep, on=["season", "player_id"])
        sub["y"] = (sub[label] == level).astype(float)
        sb, n_ps = split_half(sub, ["player_id", "season"], "y", MIN_WR_TARGETS // 4)
        yy, pairs = year_to_year(share[["player_id", "season", "value"]])
        rows.append(dict(group="WR target share", split=label, level=level, player_seasons=n_ps,
                         sb_r=round(sb, 3), yoy_r=round(yy, 3), yoy_pairs=pairs,
                         verdict=verdict(sb, yy)))

res = pd.DataFrame(rows)
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
res.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "split_stability.csv"), index=False)
print(res.to_string(index=False))

# Scheme and position requirements (draft)

Date: 2026-10-23. Status: draft for Eric. Not a fit score. Counts and summaries only.

## 1. What the requirements are

Source: `PP_Recruiting / 000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` (Baylor's recruiting grade scale). Each position has:
- Critical factors (traits). Each trait is rated on a 1 to 9 scale in the sheet.
- Measurement thresholds (height, weight and length bands by position).
- An eight-factor total that maps to grade bands (All-American 72 to 60, down to Not Good Enough under 24).

This is a recruiting and evaluation scale, not a scheme definition. It sets what a player must have. It does not say what the program runs.

## 2. Baylor offense, derived from PFF (2024 and 2025)

Source: `pff_premium` video plays. Baylor offense plays only. Shares are of all Baylor offense plays in the season.

| Item | 2024 (n = 1,153) | 2025 (n = 1,148) |
|---|---|---|
| Shotgun | 83% | 86% |
| Pistol | 0% | under 1% |
| Play action | 17% | 17% |
| No huddle | 0% | 0% |
| Pass plays (of run and pass calls) | 53% (500 of 948) | 61% (597 of 980) |
| Screen | 7% | 8% |
| Top personnel code | 3-0-1-1 (73%) | 3-0-1-1 (82%) |
| Top formations | 2x2, 3x1, 1x3 | 2x2, 3x1, 1x3 |
| Defense faced, most common | Nickel (64%) | Nickel (81%) |

Read: a shotgun, pass-leaning offense with one personnel grouping used most of the time. Run concepts are mostly blank in the feed. Coded run concepts that appear are split, cross lead and read option.

Gaps:
- Video plays exist only for 2024 and 2025 in the database. 2023 and 2026 are not covered by this read.
- Personnel codes are shown as PFF writes them. We have not confirmed the code key with PFF docs.

## 3. Requirements by position, with the PFF metric that can test each one

Only traits with a PFF link are listed. Other traits (for example size, toughness, speed) need film or measurement data, not PFF.

| Position | Scale traits (from the sheet) | PFF metric that can test it now | Not testable from PFF |
|---|---|---|---|

# STATUS

## Current state

- Draft PR #1 on branch `qb-fbs-baseline` holds all code for QB, O-line, LB, DB, RB, WR and the Power Four driver analysis.
- All models use the FBS baseline, count features only, with PFF grades as the outcome. Results are weak. No position has a usable predictor.
- Reports are in Drive `PFF_endpoint/reports/<position>/` (qb, oline, lb, db, rb, wr, drivers). Each is confirmed through the connector.

## Next

1. Decide whether to build WR receptions and yards-after-catch features, now that a receiver id is confirmed.
2. Decide whether to re-pull the charting feed with the video-play receiver field, after its id type is checked.
3. Review draft PR #1 before any merge.

## Open questions

- Outcome for the next round: keep PFF grade per game, or switch to EPA or a coach-rated outcome?
- Receiver id in the video plays feed (`pass_receiver_target`): not matched to roster ids yet. Id type unknown.
- Whether to add opponent strength to WR, LB, DB and RB (done for QB only).

## Gotchas

- Receiver link: premium passing `target_player_id` matches a WR grade row in the same game for only about 48% to 56% of target ids. The rest are TEs, RBs or others.
- Field roles are unverified against the PFF docs: `tackler_player_id`, `pass_rush` `player_id`, `runner_player_id`, `target_player_id`, and the premium `all_blocking` and `pressure` ids.
- The 2023 WR pull had 2 failed game calls (426 of 428 read). Not re-pulled.
- Scratch venv and probe scripts live outside the repo (in the session scratchpad). Only pull and model scripts are committed.
- Git: an automatic session-end commit (not from the user) added two scripts earlier. Its message is generic.

He served as the head coach at [Texas State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_State_University "Texas State University") from 2019 to 2022. ## Coaching career \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Coaching career")\] ### Early coaching career \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Early coaching career")\] Following his playing career at [Missouri State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_State_University "Missouri State University"), Spavital became a member of the coaching staff at [Tulsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Golden_Hurricane_football "Tulsa Golden Hurricane football") in 2008 where he worked as an offensive quality control assistant under [Gus Malzahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Malzahn "Gus Malzahn"). Following the 2008 season Spavital became a [graduate assistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graduate_assistant "Graduate assistant") at [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Cougars_football "Houston Cougars football"). While at Houston, Spavital worked under head coach [Kevin Sumlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Sumlin "Kevin Sumlin") and offensive coordinator [Dana Holgorsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_Holgorsen "Dana Holgorsen"). Spavital became familiar with Holgorsen's offense while working at Houston, and when Holgorsen became the offensive coordinator at [Oklahoma State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_State_Cowboys_football "Oklahoma State Cowboys football") in 2010 he took Spavital with him and gave him the same position of graduate assistant. Spavital was an essential piece of Holgorsen's coaching staff at Oklahoma State because he was the only person on the staff familiar with the offense that Holgorsen ran. Spavital helped teach the new offense to QB [Brandon Weeden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Weeden "Brandon Weeden"), who was nearly two years older than Spavital. That [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Oklahoma_State_Cowboys_football_team "2010 Oklahoma State Cowboys football team"), Oklahoma State went 11–2 and Weeden was third in the nation in yards per game and total yards as well as sixth in the nation in touchdowns.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-2) When Holgorsen became head coach at [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_football "West Virginia Mountaineers football") before the 2011 season, he took Spavital with him and made him quarterbacks coach. While at West Virginia, Spavital coached [Geno Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geno_Smith "Geno Smith"). Under Spavital's coaching Smith would break numerous [WVU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_University "West Virginia University"), NCAA, and bowl records. When Texas A&M offensive coordinator [Kliff Kingsbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kliff_Kingsbury "Kliff Kingsbury") left Texas A&M to become the head coach at [Texas Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Tech_Red_Raiders_football "Texas Tech Red Raiders football"), A&M head coach Kevin Sumlin offered Spavital the position.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-3) At Texas A&M, Spavital started as the co-offensive coordinator with Clarence McKinney and was the quarterbacks coach. In the 2013 season, he coached [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") winner [Johnny Manziel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Manziel "Johnny Manziel"). On January 3, 2016, Spavital and Texas A&M mutually parted ways, partially due to the [Kyler Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyler_Murray "Kyler Murray")/ [Kyle Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Allen_(American_football) "Kyle Allen (American football)") quarterback controversy during the 2015 season that saw both highly rated QBs transfer out of A&M the same season.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-4) On February 11, 2016, Spavital was announced as the offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach for the [California Golden Bears football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Golden_Bears_football "California Golden Bears football") team. On January 8, 2017, following the firing of head coach [Sonny Dykes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonny_Dykes "Sonny Dykes"), it was announced that Spavital would serve as interim head coach at Cal.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-5) On January 13, 2017, it was announced that Spavital would be returning to West Virginia as offensive coordinator, rejoining Holgorsen and offensive line coach Joe Wickline, who he coached with while with Holgorsen at Oklahoma State. ### Texas State \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: Texas State")\] On November 28, 2018, Spavital was named the head coach at Texas State, taking over for [Everett Withers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everett_Withers "Everett Withers").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-6) On August 29, 2019, Spavital and Texas State lost to No. 12 ranked [Texas A&M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_Aggies_football "Texas A&M Aggies football") 41–7 in Spavital's first game as head coach. On September 21, Spavital recorded his first win as a head coach when his Bobcats defeated [Georgia State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_State_Panthers_football "Georgia State Panthers football"), 37–34, in 3 OTs. Texas State fired Spavital following the 2022 season.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-7) In four years, Spavital's teams went 13–35 overall and did not appear in a [bowl game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowl_game "Bowl game"). ### Return to California \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Return to California")\] On December 6, 2022, Spavital was rehired as the offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at California, now under head coach [Justin Wilcox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Wilcox_(American_football) "Justin Wilcox (American football)").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-8) ### Baylor \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Baylor")\] On November 30, 2023, Spavital was named offensive coordinator at Baylor, under head coach [Dave Aranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Aranda "Dave Aranda").[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-9) ## Personal \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: Personal")\] Spavital's grandfather, [Jim Spavital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Spavital "Jim Spavital"), was a professional football player who played in the [All-America Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-America_Football_Conference "All-America Football Conference") (AAFC), [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL), and the [Canadian Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Football_League "Canadian Football League") (CFL) and later worked as a coach. His father is Steve Spavital, who is a former head football coach at [Broken Arrow High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broken_Arrow_High_School "Broken Arrow High School").[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-10) His brother, Zac Spavital, was the defensive coordinator under him at Texas State. ##
