1985) is an American [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") coach who is the offensive coordinator for the [Baylor Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baylor_Bears_football "Baylor Bears football"). He served as the head coach at [Texas State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_State_University "Texas State University") from 2019 to 2022. ## Coaching career \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Coaching career")\] ### Early coaching career \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Early coaching career")\] Following his playing career at [Missouri State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_State_University "Missouri State University"), Spavital became a member of the coaching staff at [Tulsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Golden_Hurricane_football "Tulsa Golden Hurricane football") in 2008 where he worked as an offensive quality control assistant under [Gus Malzahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Malzahn "Gus Malzahn"). Following the 2008 season Spavital became a [graduate assistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graduate_assistant "Graduate assistant") at [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Cougars_football "Houston Cougars football"). While at Houston, Spavital worked under head coach [Kevin Sumlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Sumlin "Kevin Sumlin") and offensive coordinator [Dana Holgorsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_Holgorsen "Dana Holgorsen"). Spavital became familiar with Holgorsen's offense while working at Houston, and when Holgorsen became the offensive coordinator at [Oklahoma State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_State_Cowboys_football "Oklahoma State Cowboys football") in 2010 he took Spavital with him and gave him the same position of graduate assistant. Spavital was an essential piece of Holgorsen's coaching staff at Oklahoma State because he was the only person on the staff familiar with the offense that Holgorsen ran. Spavital helped teach the new offense to QB [Brandon Weeden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Weeden "Brandon Weeden"), who was nearly two years older than Spavital. That [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Oklahoma_State_Cowboys_football_team "2010 Oklahoma State Cowboys football team"), Oklahoma State went 11–2 and Weeden was third in the nation in yards per game and total yards as well as sixth in the nation in touchdowns.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-2) When Holgorsen became head coach at [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_football "West Virginia Mountaineers football") before the 2011 season, he took Spavital with him and made him quarterbacks coach. While at West Virginia, Spavital coached [Geno Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geno_Smith "Geno Smith"). Under Spavital's coaching Smith would break numerous [WVU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_University "West Virginia University"), NCAA, and bowl records. When Texas A&M offensive coordinator [Kliff Kingsbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kliff_Kingsbury "Kliff Kingsbury") left Texas A&M to become the head coach at [Texas Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Tech_Red_Raiders_football "Texas Tech Red Raiders football"), A&M head coach Kevin Sumlin offered Spavital the position.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-3) At Texas A&M, Spavital started as the co-offensive coordinator with Clarence McKinney and was the quarterbacks coach. In the 2013 season, he coached [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") winner [Johnny Manziel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Manziel "Johnny Manziel"). On January 3, 2016, Spavital and Texas A&M mutually parted ways, partially due to the [Kyler Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyler_Murray "Kyler Murray")/ [Kyle Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Allen_(American_football) "Kyle Allen (American football)") quarterback controversy during the 2015 season that saw both highly rated QBs transfer out of A&M the same season.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-4) On February 11, 2016, Spavital was announced as the offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach for the [California Golden Bears football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Golden_Bears_football "California Golden Bears football") team. On January 8, 2017, following the firing of head coach [Sonny Dykes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonny_Dykes "Sonny Dykes"), it was announced that Spavital would serve as interim head coach at Cal.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-5) On January 13, 2017, it was announced that Spavital would be returning to West Virginia as offensive coordinator, rejoining Holgorsen and offensive line coach Joe Wickline, who he coached with while with Holgorsen at Oklahoma State. ### Texas State \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: Texas State")\] On November 28, 2018, Spavital was named the head coach at Texas State, taking over for [Everett Withers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everett_Withers "Everett Withers").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-6) On August 29, 2019, Spavital and Texas State lost to No. 12 ranked [Texas A&M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_Aggies_football "Texas A&M Aggies football") 41–7 in Spavital's first game as head coach. On September 21, Spavital recorded his first win as a head coach when his Bobcats defeated [Georgia State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_State_Panthers_football "Georgia State Panthers football"), 37–34, in 3 OTs. Texas State fired Spavital following the 2022 season.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-7) In four years, Spavital's teams went 13–35 overall and did not appear in a [bowl game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowl_game "Bowl game"). ### Return to California \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Return to California")\] On December 6, 2022, Spavital was rehired as the offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at California, now under head coach [Justin Wilcox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Wilcox_(American_football) "Justin Wilcox (American football)").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-8) ### Baylor \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Baylor")\] On November 30, 2023, Spavital was named offensive coordinator at Baylor, under head coach [Dave Aranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Aranda "Dave Aranda").[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-9) ## Personal \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: Personal")\] Spavital's grandfather, [Jim Spavital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Spavital "Jim Spavital"), was a professional football player who played in the [All-America Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-America_Football_Conference "All-America Football Conference") (AAFC), [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL), and the [Canadian Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Football_League "Canadian Football League") (CFL) and later worked as a coach. His father is Steve Spavital, who is a former head football coach at [Broken Arrow High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broken_Arrow_High_School "Broken Arrow High School").[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-10) His brother, Zac Spavital, was the defensive coordinator under him at Texas State. ## 1985) is an American [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") coach who is the offensive coordinator for the [Baylor Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baylor_Bears_football "Baylor Bears football"). He served as the head coach at [Texas State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_State_University "Texas State University") from 2019 to 2022. ## Coaching career \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Coaching career")\] ### Early coaching career \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Early coaching career")\] Following his playing career at [Missouri State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_State_University "Missouri State University"), Spavital became a member of the coaching staff at [Tulsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Golden_Hurricane_football "Tulsa Golden Hurricane football") in 2008 where he worked as an offensive quality control assistant under [Gus Malzahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Malzahn "Gus Malzahn"). Following the 2008 season Spavital became a [graduate assistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graduate_assistant "Graduate assistant") at [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Cougars_football "Houston Cougars football"). While at Houston, Spavital worked under head coach [Kevin Sumlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Sumlin "Kevin Sumlin") and offensive coordinator [Dana Holgorsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_Holgorsen "Dana Holgorsen"). Spavital became familiar with Holgorsen's offense while working at Houston, and when Holgorsen became the offensive coordinator at [Oklahoma State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_State_Cowboys_football "Oklahoma State Cowboys football") in 2010 he took Spavital with him and gave him the same position of graduate assistant. Spavital was an essential piece of Holgorsen's coaching staff at Oklahoma State because he was the only person on the staff familiar with the offense that Holgorsen ran. Spavital helped teach the new offense to QB [Brandon Weeden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Weeden "Brandon Weeden"), who was nearly two years older than Spavital. That [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Oklahoma_State_Cowboys_football_team "2010 Oklahoma State Cowboys football team"), Oklahoma State went 11–2 and Weeden was third in the nation in yards per game and total yards as well as sixth in the nation in touchdowns.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-2) When Holgorsen became head coach at [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_football "West Virginia Mountaineers football") before the 2011 season, he took Spavital with him and made him quarterbacks coach. While at West Virginia, Spavital coached [Geno Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geno_Smith "Geno Smith"). Under Spavital's coaching Smith would break numerous [WVU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_University "West Virginia University"), NCAA, and bowl records. When Texas A&M offensive coordinator [Kliff Kingsbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kliff_Kingsbury "Kliff Kingsbury") left Texas A&M to become the head coach at [Texas Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Tech_Red_Raiders_football "Texas Tech Red Raiders football"), A&M head coach Kevin Sumlin offered Spavital the position.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-3) At Texas A&M, Spavital started as the co-offensive coordinator with Clarence McKinney and was the quarterbacks coach. In the 2013 season, he coached [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") winner [Johnny Manziel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Manziel "Johnny Manziel"). On January 3, 2016, Spavital and Texas A&M mutually parted ways, partially due to the [Kyler Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyler_Murray "Kyler Murray")/ [Kyle Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Allen_(American_football) "Kyle Allen (American football)") quarterback controversy during the 2015 season that saw both highly rated QBs transfer out of A&M the same season.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-4) On February 11, 2016, Spavital was announced as the offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach for the [California Golden Bears football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Golden_Bears_football "California Golden Bears football") team. On January 8, 2017, following the firing of head coach [Sonny Dykes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonny_Dykes "Sonny Dykes"), it was announced that Spavital would serve as interim head coach at Cal.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-5) On January 13, 2017, it was announced that Spavital would be returning to West Virginia as offensive coordinator, rejoining Holgorsen and offensive line coach Joe Wickline, who he coached with while with Holgorsen at Oklahoma State. ### Texas State \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: Texas State")\] On November 28, 2018, Spavital was named the head coach at Texas State, taking over for [Everett Withers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everett_Withers "Everett Withers").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-6) On August 29, 2019, Spavital and Texas State lost to No. 12 ranked [Texas A&M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_Aggies_football "Texas A&M Aggies football") 41–7 in Spavital's first game as head coach. On September 21, Spavital recorded his first win as a head coach when his Bobcats defeated [Georgia State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_State_Panthers_football "Georgia State Panthers football"), 37–34, in 3 OTs. Texas State fired Spavital following the 2022 season.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-7) In four years, Spavital's teams went 13–35 overall and did not appear in a [bowl game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowl_game "Bowl game"). ### Return to California \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Return to California")\] On December 6, 2022, Spavital was rehired as the offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at California, now under head coach [Justin Wilcox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Wilcox_(American_football) "Justin Wilcox (American football)").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-8) ### Baylor \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Baylor")\] On November 30, 2023, Spavital was named offensive coordinator at Baylor, under head coach [Dave Aranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Aranda "Dave Aranda").[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-9) ## Personal \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jake_Spavital&action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: Personal")\] Spavital's grandfather, [Jim Spavital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Spavital "Jim Spavital"), was a professional football player who played in the [All-America Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-America_Football_Conference "All-America Football Conference") (AAFC), [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL), and the [Canadian Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Football_League "Canadian Football League") (CFL) and later worked as a coach. His father is Steve Spavital, who is a former head football coach at [Broken Arrow High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broken_Arrow_High_School "Broken Arrow High School").[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Spavital#cite_note-10) His brother, Zac Spavital, was the defensive coordinator under him at Texas State. ## # Scheme and position requirements (draft)

Date: 2026-10-23. Status: draft for Eric. Not a fit score. Counts and summaries only.

## 1. What the requirements are

Source: `PP_Recruiting / 000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` (Baylor's recruiting grade scale). Each position has:
- Critical factors (traits). Each trait is rated on a 1 to 9 scale in the sheet.
- Measurement thresholds (height, weight and length bands by position).
- An eight-factor total that maps to grade bands (All-American 72 to 60, down to Not Good Enough under 24).

This is a recruiting and evaluation scale, not a scheme definition. It sets what a player must have. It does not say what the program runs.

## 2. Baylor offense, derived from PFF (2024 and 2025)

Source: `pff_premium` video plays. Baylor offense plays only. Shares are of all Baylor offense plays in the season.

| Item | 2024 (n = 1,153) | 2025 (n = 1,148) |
|---|---|---|
| Shotgun | 83% | 86% |
| Pistol | 0% | under 1% |
| Play action | 17% | 17% |
| No huddle | 0% | 0% |
| Pass plays (of run and pass calls) | 53% (500 of 948) | 61% (597 of 980) |
| Screen | 7% | 8% |
| Top personnel code | 3-0-1-1 (73%) | 3-0-1-1 (82%) |
| Top formations | 2x2, 3x1, 1x3 | 2x2, 3x1, 1x3 |
| Defense faced, most common | Nickel (64%) | Nickel (81%) |

Read: a shotgun, pass-leaning offense with one personnel grouping used most of the time. Run concepts are mostly blank in the feed. Coded run concepts that appear are split, cross lead and read option.

Gaps:
- Video plays exist only for 2024 and 2025 in the database. 2023 and 2026 are not covered by this read.
- Personnel codes are shown as PFF writes them. We have not confirmed the code key with PFF docs.

## 3. Requirements by position, with the PFF metric that can test each one

Only traits with a PFF link are listed. Other traits (for example size, toughness, speed) need film or measurement data, not PFF.

| Position | Scale traits (from the sheet) | PFF metric that can test it now | Not testable from PFF |
|---|---|---|---|
| OT | Edge protection, anchor, bend, foot speed | Pressure rate on pass-pro rows (proxy) | Size, toughness |
| OG and C | Anchor, pulling, second-level blocking | Pressure rate; run-block grade (reference) | Pulling, second-level blocking |
| WR and slot | Suddenness and route running, ball skills and hands, YAC | Target share; drops; yards after catch (pff_stats) | Separation grade, route depth |
| TE | Blocking, catch in traffic | Targets; run-block grade (reference) | Blocking grade is not in the profile yet |
| RB | Contact balance, YAC, cutting, vision | Runs per snap; yards after contact (pff_stats) | Vision, cutting |
| END and JACK | Pass rush, tackling, strength at point of attack | Pass rush per snap; tackles per snap | Tackling quality, strength |
| DT | Leverage, use of hands, pad level | Tackles per snap; pass rush per snap (DI, weak) | Leverage, hands |
| ILB | Tackling, range, pass rush | Tackles per snap; pass rush per snap | Range |
| CB and STAR | Man coverage, ball skills, tackling | Burns, targets against (defensive_targets) | Man coverage grade |
| SAF | Range, key and diagnose, run support | Tackles per snap; missed tackles | Range, keying |
| QB | Accuracy, decisions, escapability | QB charting: pass accuracy, throw type | Anticipation, timing (not charted here) |

## 4. How the scheme and requirements combine (planned, not built)

- Scheme fit: a player's profile by scheme cell (for example OL pressure in shotgun, WR share on passing downs), compared with the same cell for the FBS baseline.
- Programmatic fit: the situation-adjusted profile compared with the position requirement above (for example edge pass rush per snap against the END pass-rush trait).
- Each fit output carries its sample size and reliability. Use the rule: split-half at least 0.6 and year-to-year at least 0.4.

## 5. Step 1 test result (summary)

Script: `scripts/split_stability.py`. Output: `data/split_stability.csv`. Non-Baylor rows, 2023 to 2026.

- OL pressure, all rows: split-half 0.59, year-to-year 0.55. Verdict: use with shrinkage.
- OL pressure, shotgun: split-half 0.59, year-to-year 0.52. No gain over all rows. Under-center cell too small (3 player-seasons).
- OL pressure, passing down vs standard: split-half 0.65 and 0.62. Year-to-year cannot be computed (22 and 26 pairs, under the 40 needed).
- WR target share, shotgun: split-half 0.55, year-to-year 0.29. Verdict: use with shrinkage on split-half, but year-to-year is below 0.4.
- WR target share, passing down: split-half 0.30. Verdict: exclude. The standard cell is the complement, so its numbers match.

Conclusion: the shotgun and down-and-distance splits do not clear the rule. The data is too thin for year-to-year. Do not use these splits in published profiles yet.

## 6. Open decisions for Eric

1. Use the GRD SCALE thresholds as written, or re-weight the eight factors to PFF-testable traits only?
2. Accept the pressure proxy (time to pressure), or wait for a true pressure flag?
3. Pull the 2023 and 2026 video plays so the scheme read covers all four seasons?

# Scheme and position requirements (draft)

Date: 2026-10-23. Status: draft for Eric. Not a fit score. Counts and summaries only.

## 1. What the requirements are

Source: `PP_Recruiting / 000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` (Baylor's recruiting grade scale). Each position has:
- Critical factors (traits). Each trait is rated on a 1 to 9 scale in the sheet.
- Measurement thresholds (height, weight and length bands by position).
- An eight-factor total that maps to grade bands (All-American 72 to 60, down to Not Good Enough under 24).

This is a recruiting and evaluation scale, not a scheme definition. It sets what a player must have. It does not say what the program runs.

## 2. Baylor offense, derived from PFF (2024 and 2025)

Source: `pff_premium` video plays. Baylor offense plays only. Shares are of all Baylor offense plays in the season.

| Item | 2024 (n = 1,153) | 2025 (n = 1,148) |
|---|---|---|
| Shotgun | 83% | 86% |
| Pistol | 0% | under 1% |
| Play action | 17% | 17% |
| No huddle | 0% | 0% |
| Pass plays (of run and pass calls) | 53% (500 of 948) | 61% (597 of 980) |
| Screen | 7% | 8% |
| Top personnel code | 3-0-1-1 (73%) | 3-0-1-1 (82%) |
| Top formations | 2x2, 3x1, 1x3 | 2x2, 3x1, 1x3 |
| Defense faced, most common | Nickel (64%) | Nickel (81%) |

Read: a shotgun, pass-leaning offense with one personnel grouping used most of the time. Run concepts are mostly blank in the feed. Coded run concepts that appear are split, cross lead and read option.

Gaps:
- Video plays exist only for 2024 and 2025 in the database. 2023 and 2026 are not covered by this read.
- Personnel codes are shown as PFF writes them. We have not confirmed the code key with PFF docs.

## 3. OC background and scheme lineage

Sources: Wikipedia, "Jake Spavital" (checked 2026-10-23), and Baylor Lariat, August 2024 (as given in the brief; not re-checked here).

Career (Wikipedia):
- 2008: Tulsa, offensive quality control under Gus Malzahn.
- 2009: Houston, graduate assistant under Kevin Sumlin and Dana Holgorsen.
- 2010: Oklahoma State, graduate assistant under Holgorsen. Brandon Weeden was third in the nation in yards per game and total yards.
- 2011 to 2012: West Virginia, quarterbacks coach under Holgorsen (Geno Smith).
- 2013 to 2015: Texas A&M, co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach (2013: Johnny Manziel). Offensive coordinator from 2014.
- 2016: California, offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach. Interim head coach in January 2017.
- 2017 to 2018: West Virginia, offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach under Holgorsen.
- 2019 to 2022: Texas State, head coach. Record 13 to 35.
- 2023: California, offensive coordinator under Justin Wilcox (rehired December 2022).
- 2024 to present: Baylor, offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach under Dave Aranda. Announced November 30, 2023.

Scheme lineage (inference, not confirmed by a source):
- The Holgorsen tree (Oklahoma State, West Virginia, Texas A&M) is the most likely base. Wikipedia says he took Holgorsen's offense to each stop. Neither source describes any stop's offense in detail.

Baylor change in 2024 (Baylor Lariat, August 2024, as given in the brief):
- Up-tempo spread, more downfield passing, fewer tight ends, receiver-driven.
- Spavital calls plays and coaches quarterbacks.
- Check against the PFF scheme read in section 2: shotgun about 85% and pass share 53% to 61% fit a spread, pass-leaning offense.

## 4. Requirements by position, with the PFF metric that can test each one

Only traits with a PFF link are listed. Other traits (for example size, toughness, speed) need film or measurement data, not PFF.

| Position | Scale traits (from the sheet) | PFF metric that can test it now | Not testable from PFF |
|---|---|---|---|
| OT | Edge protection, anchor, bend, foot speed | Pressure rate on pass-pro rows (proxy) | Size, toughness |
| OG and C | Anchor, pulling, second-level blocking | Pressure rate; run-block grade (reference) | Pulling, second-level blocking |
| WR and slot | Suddenness and route running, ball skills and hands, YAC | Target share; drops; yards after catch (pff_stats) | Separation grade, route depth |
| TE | Blocking, catch in traffic | Targets; run-block grade (reference) | Blocking grade is not in the profile yet |
| RB | Contact balance, YAC, cutting, vision | Runs per snap; yards after contact (pff_stats) | Vision, cutting |
| END and JACK | Pass rush, tackling, strength at point of attack | Pass rush per snap; tackles per snap | Tackling quality, strength |
| DT | Leverage, use of hands, pad level | Tackles per snap; pass rush per snap (DI, weak) | Leverage, hands |
| ILB | Tackling, range, pass rush | Tackles per snap; pass rush per snap | Range |
| CB and STAR | Man coverage, ball skills, tackling | Burns, targets against (defensive_targets) | Man coverage grade |
| SAF | Range, key and diagnose, run support | Tackles per snap; missed tackles | Range, keying |
| QB | Accuracy, decisions, escapability | QB charting: pass accuracy, throw type | Anticipation, timing (not charted here) |

## 4. How the scheme and requirements combine (planned, not built)

- Scheme fit: a player's profile by scheme cell (for example OL pressure in shotgun, WR share on passing downs), compared with the same cell for the FBS baseline.
- Programmatic fit: the situation-adjusted profile compared with the position requirement above (for example edge pass rush per snap against the END pass-rush trait).
- Each fit output carries its sample size and reliability. Use the rule: split-half at least 0.6 and year-to-year at least 0.4.

## 5. Step 1 test result (summary)

Script: `scripts/split_stability.py`. Output: `data/split_stability.csv`. Non-Baylor rows, 2023 to 2026.

- OL pressure, all rows: split-half 0.59, year-to-year 0.55. Verdict: use with shrinkage.
- OL pressure, shotgun: split-half 0.59, year-to-year 0.52. No gain over all rows. Under-center cell too small (3 player-seasons).
- OL pressure, passing down vs standard: split-half 0.65 and 0.62. Year-to-year cannot be computed (22 and 26 pairs, under the 40 needed).
- WR target share, shotgun: split-half 0.55, year-to-year 0.29. Verdict: use with shrinkage on split-half, but year-to-year is below 0.4.
- WR target share, passing down: split-half 0.30. Verdict: exclude. The standard cell is the complement, so its numbers match.

Conclusion: the shotgun and down-and-distance splits do not clear the rule. The data is too thin for year-to-year. Do not use these splits in published profiles yet.

## 6. Open decisions for Eric

1. Use the GRD SCALE thresholds as written, or re-weight the eight factors to PFF-testable traits only?
2. Accept the pressure proxy (time to pressure), or wait for a true pressure flag?
3. Pull the 2023 and 2026 video plays so the scheme read covers all four seasons?

# PFF Data Project

Local data pipeline that ingests Pro Football Focus (PFF) game and player data
into a DuckDB database, scoped to Baylor University Football plus every Big 12
and non-conference opponent for the current season and two prior.

The database is the deliverable. Visualization, cross-system athlete joins, and
AMS-style reporting are the responsibility of downstream projects.

## Status

**Phase 0 complete; pipeline implemented and verified against the live API.**
Auth, the ingest pipeline, shapers, and a DuckDB schema are working. The full API
contract is documented in `docs/pff_api_notes.md` (OpenAPI specs in
`docs/swagger/`). Verified end-to-end: a real Baylor game pulled 485 player-grade
rows across 11 grade types into the DB.

What works: `--dry-run` (auth + scope), per-game/per-season/weekly grade ingest,
extended stats, premium feeds (as keyed JSON), idempotent upserts. Player-tracking
feeds are a deliberate future addition (see notes).

## Setup

Requires Python 3.12+ and PFF API credentials.

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/Scripts/activate    # Windows Git Bash; use .venv/bin/activate on macOS/Linux
pip install -r requirements.txt

cp .env.example .env
# Fill in PFF_BASE_URL, PFF_API_KEY, and BAYLOR_TEAM_ID
```

Activate the shared pre-commit hook (keeps `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in sync):

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

"""Pull full seasons of the PFF video plays feed into slim per-play Parquet files.

    python scripts/pull_season_video_plays.py --season 2024 --season 2025

Writes data/video_plays_slim_<season>.parquet (gitignored). A season whose file
already exists is skipped unless --refresh is passed. The feed is ~2.5 GB per
season decoded and streams in about a minute; see src/ingest/season_plays.py.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

import yaml  # noqa: E402
from dotenv import load_dotenv  # noqa: E402

from src.ingest import pipeline, season_plays  # noqa: E402


def destination(season: int) -> Path:
    return ROOT / "data" / f"video_plays_slim_{season}.parquet"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--season", type=int, action="append", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--refresh", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    load_dotenv(ROOT / ".env")
    config = yaml.safe_load((ROOT / "config" / "pipeline.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    client = pipeline._client(config)

    for season in args.season:
        games_path = ROOT / "data" / f"video_games_{season}.parquet"
        if not games_path.exists() or args.refresh:
            games = season_plays.fetch_games(client, season)
            season_plays.write_parquet(games, games_path)
            print(f"{season}: {len(games):,} games, "
                  f"{int(games['home_team_score'].notna().sum()):,} with final scores "
                  f"-> {games_path.name}")

        path = destination(season)
        if path.exists() and not args.refresh:
            print(f"{season}: {path.name} exists, skipped (pass --refresh to re-pull)")
            continue
        started = time.time()
        frame = season_plays.to_frame(season_plays.stream_season(client, season))
        rows = season_plays.write_parquet(frame, path)
        print(f"{season}: {rows:,} plays, {frame['game_id'].nunique():,} games, "
              f"{time.time() - started:.0f}s -> {path.name}")
    return 0

        print(f"{season}: {rows:,} plays, {frame['game_id'].nunique():,} games, "

import duckdb
import ijson
import pandas as pd
import requests

EPA_FIELDS = [
    "expected_points",
    "expected_points_added",
    "expected_points_legacy",
    "expected_points_added_legacy",
]

FIELDS = [
    "game_id", "play_id", "season", "week", "game_date",
    "home_team", "away_team", "offense", "defense",
    "quarter", "clock", "down", "distance", "yards_to_goal_line",
    "run_pass", "special_teams_type", "no_play", "penalty", "turnover",
    "garbage_time", "score", "off_score", "def_score", "home_score", "away_score",
    "drive", "drive_end_event",
    *EPA_FIELDS,
]

SEASON_PATH = "/v1/video/{league}/{season}/plays"
STREAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 600


def slim(play: dict) -> dict:
    """Keep only FIELDS. A field PFF omitted (it omits zero values) is None."""
    return {field: play.get(field) for field in FIELDS}


def iter_plays(stream: IO[bytes]) -> Iterator[dict]:
    """Yield each object in the payload's `plays` array without loading the rest."""
    yield from ijson.items(stream, "plays.item", use_float=True)


def _text(value) -> str | None:
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and value != value):
        return None
    return str(value)


def to_frame(plays: Iterable[dict]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    rows = [slim(play) for play in plays]
    # dtype=object keeps each value as parsed. Without it pandas turns a column
    # of ints with a gap into float64, and the text becomes "2.0" and "nan".
    frame = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=FIELDS, dtype=object)
    for field in FIELDS:
        if field in EPA_FIELDS:
            frame[field] = pd.to_numeric(frame[field], errors="coerce")
        else:
            frame[field] = frame[field].map(_text)
    return frame


def write_parquet(frame: pd.DataFrame, destination: Path) -> int:
    """Write via a temp file so an interrupted run never leaves a half file."""
    destination = Path(destination)
    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    partial = destination.with_suffix(destination.suffix + ".partial")
    con = duckdb.connect()
    try:
        con.register("plays", frame)
        con.execute(f"COPY plays TO '{partial}' (FORMAT PARQUET)")
    finally:
        con.close()
    os.replace(partial, destination)
    return len(frame)


def stream_season(client, season: int) -> Iterator[dict]:
    """Open the season feed with the client's token and yield plays as they arrive."""
    client._ensure_token()
    url = client.base_url + SEASON_PATH.format(league=client.league, season=season)
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {client._token}",
        "Accept": "application/json",
        "Accept-Encoding": "gzip",
    }
    with requests.get(url, headers=headers, stream=True,
                      timeout=STREAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) as resp:
        resp.raise_for_status()
        resp.raw.decode_content = True
        yield from iter_plays(resp.raw)


GAME_FIELDS = [
    "id", "season", "week", "start", "home_team", "away_team",
    "home_team_score", "away_team_score",
]

        yield from iter_plays(resp.raw)

# PFF Data Project — Agent Guide

This file is the canonical project memory for any AI coding agent working in this
repo. It is mirrored verbatim into `AGENTS.md` so OpenAI Codex (and any other
agent that reads `AGENTS.md`) gets the same context. A pre-commit hook in
`.githooks/pre-commit` blocks commits where the two files diverge.

If you edit one, edit both. See "Keeping CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in sync" below.

---

## What this project is

A standalone Python data pipeline that pulls Pro Football Focus (PFF) game and
player data into a local **DuckDB** database for Baylor University Football
analysis. Scope is **Baylor + every Big 12 team + non-conference opponents** for
the **current season plus two prior**.

The DB *is* the deliverable. There are no dashboards in this repo. Downstream
consumers — Power BI, Jupyter notebooks, and a future athlete management system
(AMS) project that will unify PFF with Catapult GPS, VALD ForceDecks, and Perch
VBT data — own visualization and cross-domain joins.

## Sister pipelines (do not modify from here)

- **VALD ForceDecks (CMJ/IMTP):** `..\..\ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` — the
  architectural template this project mirrors.
- **Catapult GPS:** `..\..\DataBase_GPS_Reporting`
- **Perch VBT:** not yet built.

The pattern across all of them is: per-domain Python pipeline → per-domain DB →
future AMS layer unions them on `(athlete_id, source_system, pulled_at)`.

## Tech stack

- Python 3.12+
- `duckdb`, `requests`, `python-dotenv`, `PyJWT`, `pyyaml`, `pandas`, `pytest`
- No web framework, no ORM, no dashboard libs — keep it lean

## Layout

```
PFF_Data_Project/
├── CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md       # this file (mirrored)
├── README.md                   # user-facing setup and usage
├── requirements.txt
├── .env.example                # PFF_BASE_URL, PFF_API_KEY, BAYLOR_TEAM_ID
├── .gitignore
├── .githooks/pre-commit        # blocks CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md divergence
├── run_pipeline.py             # CLI entry
├── config/
│   └── pipeline.yaml           # team/season scope, endpoints, retry config
├── src/
│   ├── db.py                   # DuckDB schema + connect + backup helpers
│   ├── ingest/
│   │   ├── pff_client.py       # PFF HTTP client (stub until Phase 0 done)
│   │   └── pipeline.py         # Orchestration: dims → facts → log
│   └── shape/transform.py      # JSON → tidy rows (teams/games/grades/stats/premium)
├── data/                       # small extracts only; the DuckDB lives at $PFF_DB
├── docs/
│   └── pff_api_notes.md        # Phase 0 spike output
├── scripts/
│   └── phase0_probe.py         # Credential discovery probe
└── tests/
    ├── test_db.py
    └── fixtures/
```

## Data model contract

Dimensions are stable identities; facts are timestamped measurements.

- **Dimensions:** `teams`, `players`, `player_seasons`, `games`
- **Facts:** `pff_grades` (per-player per-game, long form), `pff_stats` (extended
  stats, long form), `pff_premium` (advanced metrics, keyed JSON passthrough)
- **Operational:** `ingest_log`

`players` / `player_seasons` are derived from the grade rows (which carry
player_id, name, position, team_id, season) — cleanest "who actually played"
source; avoids the giant all-NCAA `/players` pull.

Every fact row carries `source_system = 'PFF'` and `pulled_at`. This is
non-negotiable — it is the contract the future AMS layer relies on to union PFF
with Catapult, VALD, and Perch facts.

`pff_player_id` is the durable join key. This pipeline does **not** maintain a
canonical athlete master record across systems. That mapping
(`roster.athlete_id → pff_player_id`) belongs to the future AMS project. Do not
invent it here.

## API contract (Phase 0 complete)

Full contract is in `docs/pff_api_notes.md`; OpenAPI specs in `docs/swagger/`.
Essentials:

- **Auth:** `POST /auth/login` with header `x-api-key: <key>` → `{"jwt"}`. Send
  `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on all calls. JWT lasts ~1h; re-auth on 401.
  Rate-limited (HTTP 429) — client backs off. `src/ingest/pff_client.py` owns this.
- **Base:** `https://api.profootballfocus.com`, league slug `ncaa`, season = year.
- **Baylor:** team_id / franchise_id = `118` (`BAYLOR_TEAM_ID` in `.env`).
- **Scope is open:** the key reads all NCAA teams + grades for any game, so
  Baylor + Big 12 + opponents is achievable despite the token's `franchise:118`
  constraint.
- **Play-by-play exists in the Video Feeds API** (EPA fields confirmed 2026-09-13):
  `/v1/video/ncaa/games/{game_id}/plays`, 330+ fields per play, including PFF EPA
  (`expected_points_added` and `expected_points_added_legacy`). Ingested for Baylor
  2024-2025 into `pff_premium` as category `video_plays` by
  `scripts/pull_video_plays.py`; deliberately not in `PREMIUM_CATEGORIES` (the
  season loop would pull every scoped game at ~1.5 MB each).
- **Full seasons stream from `/v1/video/ncaa/{season}/plays`** (~2.5 GB decoded,
  about a minute): `scripts/pull_season_video_plays.py --season YYYY` writes
  `data/video_plays_slim_<season>.parquet` (31 fields per play) and
  `data/video_games_<season>.parquet` (final scores; the plays feed only has the
  score before each snap). Both gitignored. `season_plays.to_frame` must build
  the frame with `dtype=object`: without it an int column with a gap becomes
  float64 and is stored as the text `"2.0"` and `"nan"`.
  Premium feeds (`/v1/premium/...`) provide play-level advanced metrics → captured
  in `pff_premium` as keyed JSON passthrough. All 12 API specs are in `docs/swagger/`.
- **FUTURE:** player-tracking feeds are deliberately not modeled in v1.

## Conventions

- **Credentials never in code.** `.env` only. Loaded via `python-dotenv`. The
  `.env` file is gitignored; `.env.example` is committed as the template.
- **DuckDB upserts:** use `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO` (idempotent refresh — re-pulling
  a week updates values rather than duplicating). See `_upsert` in `pipeline.py`.
- **Config path resolution:** always anchor to `Path(__file__).resolve().parent`
  walks, never relative paths from CWD. `run_pipeline.py` and `src/db.py` show
  the pattern.
- **The DB is not in the repo.** `src/db.py` resolves it from **`$PFF_DB`**, falling
  back to the old `data/pff.db` when the variable is unset. Windows:
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pff-data\pff.db` (set 2026-09-22). Mac: `~/.local/share/pff-data/pff.db` (set 2026-10-08 in `~/.zshrc`; the Windows laptop is hands-off). Reason: `~/Desktop/DEV` is a
  two-way Google Drive mirror, and Drive re-uploads and **locks** a 500 MB file on
  every write; on 2026-09-22 it held the file open against a running pull
  (`GoogleDriveFS.exe`). Keep the DB, its WAL and its backups out of the mirrored tree.
- **Backups before destructive ops:** copy the DB to
  `pff_before_<operation>_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.db` **beside it**, not into `data/`.
  `src/db.backup_db()` does this — use it from any new destructive code path.
- **Idempotent ingests:** running the same week twice must be a no-op.
- **One concern per module.** Client does HTTP. Shape does JSON-to-rows. Pipeline
  orchestrates. db.py owns the schema. Don't blur these.
- **Tests use mocked HTTP**, not live API calls. The Phase 0 probe is the only
  script that hits the real API.
- **No comments that narrate the obvious.** Comments are for non-obvious WHYs
  (e.g., "DuckDB requires ON CONFLICT here; SQLite syntax silently fails").

## CLI commands

```
python run_pipeline.py --dry-run               # auth + scope check, no writes
python run_pipeline.py --backfill              # full 3-season pull
python run_pipeline.py --season 2025           # full season
python run_pipeline.py --season 2025 --week 8  # one week
python run_pipeline.py --diagnose [NAME]       # query local DB
python run_pipeline.py --reset-db              # backup + reinit
```

Moving data between the Mac and Windows (never re-pull what the other machine already has):

```
python scripts/export_snapshot.py              # every season -> Parquet on Drive
python scripts/export_snapshot.py --season 2026
python scripts/load_snapshot.py --dry-run      # what would change here
python scripts/load_snapshot.py                # load what Drive has
```

## Moving data between machines

The DB never travels. `git` cannot hold a 600 MB binary and a live database inside a
synced folder gets locked and re-uploaded on every write. Instead each machine keeps its
own local DB and they exchange **immutable Parquet snapshots** through Google Drive:
written once, never mutated, so a half-synced file cannot corrupt anything.

- Root: `$PFF_SNAPSHOT_DIR`, else `.../00_Primary_Storage_Drive/pff-snapshots`.
- One file per table per season (`pff_grades/season=2026.parquet`), so a single season
  moves without dragging six million rows behind it. It is small: all of 2026,
  1.33 M rows, is about 6 MB.
- `manifest.json` records rows, bytes, which machine wrote it and when. An export
  merges into it, so exporting one season never erases the record of the others.
- The load merges by primary key and never deletes: snapshot rows are added or replace
  the matching local row; rows only this machine has are kept (the dry run says how
  many). Idempotent, and it backs the DB up first. It used to delete each season first,
  which erased the Mac's video_plays on 2026-09-22; `tests/test_snapshot.py` guards it.
- `ingest_log` is never exported. It says what **this** machine fetched; copying it
  would make the other machine's history a lie.
- After `dev-sync` pulls the scripts, run `load_snapshot.py` to pull the data. Git
  carries the code, Drive carries the rows.

## Testing

```
pytest tests/
```

Tests that need a DB use a per-test temp path; don't touch `data/pff.db`.

## Keeping CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in sync

`AGENTS.md` is a byte-identical copy of `CLAUDE.md`. The pre-commit hook at
`.githooks/pre-commit` blocks commits when they differ. Activate the hook once
per clone:

```
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

When updating agent guidance, edit `CLAUDE.md` first, then:

```
cp CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
git add CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
```

If you intentionally need them to diverge (tool-specific instructions for one
agent), update the hook before committing — don't bypass it silently with
`--no-verify`.

## Working with this repo from Codex

Codex reads `AGENTS.md` automatically. Everything above applies to Codex
sessions identically. Codex-specific notes, if any are ever needed, go in a
separate section here and get mirrored.


## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

import duckdb
import ijson
import pandas as pd
import requests

EPA_FIELDS = [
    "expected_points",
    "expected_points_added",
    "expected_points_legacy",
    "expected_points_added_legacy",
]

FIELDS = [
    "game_id", "play_id", "season", "week", "game_date",
    "home_team", "away_team", "offense", "defense",
    "quarter", "clock", "down", "distance", "yards_to_goal_line",
    "run_pass", "special_teams_type", "no_play", "penalty", "turnover",
    "garbage_time", "score", "off_score", "def_score", "home_score", "away_score",
    "drive", "drive_end_event",
    *EPA_FIELDS,
]

SEASON_PATH = "/v1/video/{league}/{season}/plays"
STREAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 600


def slim(play: dict) -> dict:
    """Keep only FIELDS. A field PFF omitted (it omits zero values) is None."""
    return {field: play.get(field) for field in FIELDS}


def iter_plays(stream: IO[bytes]) -> Iterator[dict]:
    """Yield each object in the payload's `plays` array without loading the rest."""
    yield from ijson.items(stream, "plays.item", use_float=True)


def _text(value) -> str | None:
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and value != value):
        return None
    return str(value)


def to_frame(plays: Iterable[dict]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    rows = [slim(play) for play in plays]
    # dtype=object keeps each value as parsed. Without it pandas turns a column
    # of ints with a gap into float64, and the text becomes "2.0" and "nan".
    frame = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=FIELDS, dtype=object)
    for field in FIELDS:
        if field in EPA_FIELDS:
            frame[field] = pd.to_numeric(frame[field], errors="coerce")
        else:
            frame[field] = frame[field].map(_text)
    return frame


def write_parquet(frame: pd.DataFrame, destination: Path) -> int:
    """Write via a temp file so an interrupted run never leaves a half file."""
    destination = Path(destination)
    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    partial = destination.with_suffix(destination.suffix + ".partial")
    con = duckdb.connect()
    try:
        con.register("plays", frame)
        con.execute(f"COPY plays TO '{partial}' (FORMAT PARQUET)")
    finally:
        con.close()
    os.replace(partial, destination)
    return len(frame)


def stream_season(client, season: int) -> Iterator[dict]:
    """Open the season feed with the client's token and yield plays as they arrive."""
    client._ensure_token()
    url = client.base_url + SEASON_PATH.format(league=client.league, season=season)
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {client._token}",
        "Accept": "application/json",
        "Accept-Encoding": "gzip",
    }
    with requests.get(url, headers=headers, stream=True,
                      timeout=STREAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) as resp:
        resp.raise_for_status()
        resp.raw.decode_content = True
        yield from iter_plays(resp.raw)


GAME_FIELDS = [
    "id", "season", "week", "start", "home_team", "away_team",
    "home_team_score", "away_team_score",
]

# PFF Data Project — Agent Guide

This file is the canonical project memory for any AI coding agent working in this
repo. It is mirrored verbatim into `AGENTS.md` so OpenAI Codex (and any other
agent that reads `AGENTS.md`) gets the same context. A pre-commit hook in
`.githooks/pre-commit` blocks commits where the two files diverge.

If you edit one, edit both. See "Keeping CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in sync" below.

---

## What this project is

A standalone Python data pipeline that pulls Pro Football Focus (PFF) game and
player data into a local **DuckDB** database for Baylor University Football
analysis. Scope is **Baylor + every Big 12 team + non-conference opponents** for
the **current season plus two prior**.

The DB *is* the deliverable. There are no dashboards in this repo. Downstream
consumers — Power BI, Jupyter notebooks, and a future athlete management system
(AMS) project that will unify PFF with Catapult GPS, VALD ForceDecks, and Perch
VBT data — own visualization and cross-domain joins.

## Sister pipelines (do not modify from here)

- **VALD ForceDecks (CMJ/IMTP):** `..\..\ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` — the
  architectural template this project mirrors.
- **Catapult GPS:** `..\..\DataBase_GPS_Reporting`
- **Perch VBT:** not yet built.

The pattern across all of them is: per-domain Python pipeline → per-domain DB →
future AMS layer unions them on `(athlete_id, source_system, pulled_at)`.

## Tech stack

- Python 3.12+
- `duckdb`, `requests`, `python-dotenv`, `PyJWT`, `pyyaml`, `pandas`, `pytest`
- No web framework, no ORM, no dashboard libs — keep it lean

## Layout

```
PFF_Data_Project/
├── CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md       # this file (mirrored)
├── README.md                   # user-facing setup and usage
├── requirements.txt
├── .env.example                # PFF_BASE_URL, PFF_API_KEY, BAYLOR_TEAM_ID
├── .gitignore
├── .githooks/pre-commit        # blocks CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md divergence
├── run_pipeline.py             # CLI entry
├── config/
│   └── pipeline.yaml           # team/season scope, endpoints, retry config
├── src/
│   ├── db.py                   # DuckDB schema + connect + backup helpers
│   ├── ingest/
│   │   ├── pff_client.py       # PFF HTTP client (stub until Phase 0 done)
│   │   └── pipeline.py         # Orchestration: dims → facts → log
│   └── shape/transform.py      # JSON → tidy rows (teams/games/grades/stats/premium)
├── data/                       # small extracts only; the DuckDB lives at $PFF_DB
├── docs/
│   └── pff_api_notes.md        # Phase 0 spike output
├── scripts/
│   └── phase0_probe.py         # Credential discovery probe
└── tests/
    ├── test_db.py
    └── fixtures/
```

## Data model contract

Dimensions are stable identities; facts are timestamped measurements.

- **Dimensions:** `teams`, `players`, `player_seasons`, `games`
- **Facts:** `pff_grades` (per-player per-game, long form), `pff_stats` (extended
  stats, long form), `pff_premium` (advanced metrics, keyed JSON passthrough)
- **Operational:** `ingest_log`

`players` / `player_seasons` are derived from the grade rows (which carry
player_id, name, position, team_id, season) — cleanest "who actually played"
source; avoids the giant all-NCAA `/players` pull.

Every fact row carries `source_system = 'PFF'` and `pulled_at`. This is
non-negotiable — it is the contract the future AMS layer relies on to union PFF
with Catapult, VALD, and Perch facts.

`pff_player_id` is the durable join key. This pipeline does **not** maintain a
canonical athlete master record across systems. That mapping
(`roster.athlete_id → pff_player_id`) belongs to the future AMS project. Do not
invent it here.

## API contract (Phase 0 complete)

Full contract is in `docs/pff_api_notes.md`; OpenAPI specs in `docs/swagger/`.
Essentials:

- **Auth:** `POST /auth/login` with header `x-api-key: <key>` → `{"jwt"}`. Send
  `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on all calls. JWT lasts ~1h; re-auth on 401.
  Rate-limited (HTTP 429) — client backs off. `src/ingest/pff_client.py` owns this.
- **Base:** `https://api.profootballfocus.com`, league slug `ncaa`, season = year.
- **Baylor:** team_id / franchise_id = `118` (`BAYLOR_TEAM_ID` in `.env`).
- **Scope is open:** the key reads all NCAA teams + grades for any game, so
  Baylor + Big 12 + opponents is achievable despite the token's `franchise:118`
  constraint.
- **Play-by-play exists in the Video Feeds API** (EPA fields confirmed 2026-09-13):
  `/v1/video/ncaa/games/{game_id}/plays`, 330+ fields per play, including PFF EPA
  (`expected_points_added` and `expected_points_added_legacy`). Ingested for Baylor
  2024-2025 into `pff_premium` as category `video_plays` by
  `scripts/pull_video_plays.py`; deliberately not in `PREMIUM_CATEGORIES` (the
  season loop would pull every scoped game at ~1.5 MB each).
- **Full seasons stream from `/v1/video/ncaa/{season}/plays`** (~2.5 GB decoded,
  about a minute): `scripts/pull_season_video_plays.py --season YYYY` writes
  `data/video_plays_slim_<season>.parquet` (31 fields per play) and
  `data/video_games_<season>.parquet` (final scores; the plays feed only has the
  score before each snap). Both gitignored. `season_plays.to_frame` must build
  the frame with `dtype=object`: without it an int column with a gap becomes
  float64 and is stored as the text `"2.0"` and `"nan"`.
  Premium feeds (`/v1/premium/...`) provide play-level advanced metrics → captured
  in `pff_premium` as keyed JSON passthrough. All 12 API specs are in `docs/swagger/`.
- **FUTURE:** player-tracking feeds are deliberately not modeled in v1.

## Conventions

- **Credentials never in code.** `.env` only. Loaded via `python-dotenv`. The
  `.env` file is gitignored; `.env.example` is committed as the template.
- **DuckDB upserts:** use `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO` (idempotent refresh — re-pulling
  a week updates values rather than duplicating). See `_upsert` in `pipeline.py`.
- **Config path resolution:** always anchor to `Path(__file__).resolve().parent`
  walks, never relative paths from CWD. `run_pipeline.py` and `src/db.py` show
  the pattern.
- **The DB is not in the repo.** `src/db.py` resolves it from **`$PFF_DB`**, falling
  back to the old `data/pff.db` when the variable is unset. Windows:
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pff-data\pff.db` (set 2026-09-22). Mac: `~/.local/share/pff-data/pff.db` (set 2026-10-08 in `~/.zshrc`; the Windows laptop is hands-off). Reason: `~/Desktop/DEV` is a
  two-way Google Drive mirror, and Drive re-uploads and **locks** a 500 MB file on
  every write; on 2026-09-22 it held the file open against a running pull
  (`GoogleDriveFS.exe`). Keep the DB, its WAL and its backups out of the mirrored tree.
- **Backups before destructive ops:** copy the DB to
  `pff_before_<operation>_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.db` **beside it**, not into `data/`.
  `src/db.backup_db()` does this — use it from any new destructive code path.
- **Idempotent ingests:** running the same week twice must be a no-op.
- **One concern per module.** Client does HTTP. Shape does JSON-to-rows. Pipeline
  orchestrates. db.py owns the schema. Don't blur these.
- **Tests use mocked HTTP**, not live API calls. The Phase 0 probe is the only
  script that hits the real API.
- **No comments that narrate the obvious.** Comments are for non-obvious WHYs
  (e.g., "DuckDB requires ON CONFLICT here; SQLite syntax silently fails").

## CLI commands

```
python run_pipeline.py --dry-run               # auth + scope check, no writes
python run_pipeline.py --backfill              # full 3-season pull
python run_pipeline.py --season 2025           # full season
python run_pipeline.py --season 2025 --week 8  # one week
python run_pipeline.py --diagnose [NAME]       # query local DB
python run_pipeline.py --reset-db              # backup + reinit
```

Moving data between the Mac and Windows (never re-pull what the other machine already has):

```
python scripts/export_snapshot.py              # every season -> Parquet on Drive
python scripts/export_snapshot.py --season 2026
python scripts/load_snapshot.py --dry-run      # what would change here
python scripts/load_snapshot.py                # load what Drive has
```

## Moving data between machines

The DB never travels. `git` cannot hold a 600 MB binary and a live database inside a
synced folder gets locked and re-uploaded on every write. Instead each machine keeps its
own local DB and they exchange **immutable Parquet snapshots** through Google Drive:
written once, never mutated, so a half-synced file cannot corrupt anything.

- Root: `$PFF_SNAPSHOT_DIR`, else `.../00_Primary_Storage_Drive/pff-snapshots`.
- One file per table per season (`pff_grades/season=2026.parquet`), so a single season
  moves without dragging six million rows behind it. It is small: all of 2026,
  1.33 M rows, is about 6 MB.
- `manifest.json` records rows, bytes, which machine wrote it and when. An export
  merges into it, so exporting one season never erases the record of the others.
- The load merges by primary key and never deletes: snapshot rows are added or replace
  the matching local row; rows only this machine has are kept (the dry run says how
  many). Idempotent, and it backs the DB up first. It used to delete each season first,
  which erased the Mac's video_plays on 2026-09-22; `tests/test_snapshot.py` guards it.
- `ingest_log` is never exported. It says what **this** machine fetched; copying it
  would make the other machine's history a lie.
- After `dev-sync` pulls the scripts, run `load_snapshot.py` to pull the data. Git
  carries the code, Drive carries the rows.

## Testing

```
pytest tests/
```

Tests that need a DB use a per-test temp path; don't touch `data/pff.db`.

## Keeping CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in sync

`AGENTS.md` is a byte-identical copy of `CLAUDE.md`. The pre-commit hook at
`.githooks/pre-commit` blocks commits when they differ. Activate the hook once
per clone:

```
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

When updating agent guidance, edit `CLAUDE.md` first, then:

```
cp CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
git add CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
```

If you intentionally need them to diverge (tool-specific instructions for one
agent), update the hook before committing — don't bypass it silently with
`--no-verify`.

## Working with this repo from Codex

Codex reads `AGENTS.md` automatically. Everything above applies to Codex
sessions identically. Codex-specific notes, if any are ever needed, go in a
separate section here and get mirrored.


## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

"""Baylor offensive scheme read from the full PFF video-plays season stream, 2023 to 2026.

Streams each season with the PFF_Data_Project client (read-only, nothing saved raw), keeps only
Baylor offense plays, and writes shares to data/scheme_read_<season>.csv. Output is counts and
shares only. The raw play rows are not written anywhere.

shortcut: fields are read as PFF writes them (shotgun 'S', personnel code as given). The personnel
code key is not checked against PFF docs.
"""
import os
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import yaml

PROJECT = Path(os.environ.get("PFF_DATA_PROJECT", "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Football/PFF_Data_Project"))
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data"
BAYLOR = "TXBA"
SEASONS = [2023, 2024, 2025, 2026]

sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT))
from dotenv import load_dotenv  # noqa: E402
from src.ingest import pipeline, season_plays  # noqa: E402


def shares(counter: Counter, total: int) -> dict:
    return {k: round(v / total, 4) for k, v in counter.most_common()} if total else {}


def read_season(client, season: int) -> dict:
    plays = 0
    cols = {k: Counter() for k in ["shotgun", "pistol", "play_action", "no_huddle", "run_pass",
                                   "screen", "personnel", "formation", "def_package"]}
    for play in season_plays.stream_season(client, season):
        if play.get("offense") != BAYLOR:
            continue
        plays += 1
        cols["shotgun"][play.get("shotgun") or "under_center"] += 1
        cols["pistol"][play.get("pistol") or "none"] += 1
        cols["play_action"][str(play.get("play_action") or 0)] += 1
        cols["no_huddle"][str(play.get("no_huddle") or 0)] += 1
        cols["run_pass"][play.get("run_pass") or "blank"] += 1
        cols["screen"][str(play.get("screen") or 0)] += 1
        cols["personnel"][play.get("offensive_personnel") or "blank"] += 1
        cols["formation"][play.get("offensive_formation_group") or "blank"] += 1
        cols["def_package"][play.get("def_package") or "blank"] += 1
    rows = []
    for name, counter in cols.items():
        for level, n in counter.most_common():
            rows.append({"season": season, "field": name, "level": level, "plays": n,
                         "share": round(n / plays, 4) if plays else None})
    return {"season": season, "baylor_plays": plays, "rows": rows}


def main() -> None:
    load_dotenv(PROJECT / ".env")
    config = yaml.safe_load((PROJECT / "config" / "pipeline.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    client = pipeline._client(config)
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    summary = []
    for season in SEASONS:
        result = read_season(client, season)
        pd.DataFrame(result["rows"]).to_csv(OUT / f"scheme_read_{season}.csv", index=False)
        summary.append((season, result["baylor_plays"]))
        print(f"{season}: {result['baylor_plays']:,} Baylor offense plays -> data/scheme_read_{season}.csv")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Scheme and position requirements (draft)

Date: 2026-10-23. Status: draft for Eric. Not a fit score. Counts and summaries only.

## 1. What the requirements are

Source: `PP_Recruiting / 000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` (Baylor's recruiting grade scale). Each position has:
- Critical factors (traits). Each trait is rated on a 1 to 9 scale in the sheet.
- Measurement thresholds (height, weight and length bands by position).
- An eight-factor total that maps to grade bands (All-American 72 to 60, down to Not Good Enough under 24).

This is a recruiting and evaluation scale, not a scheme definition. It sets what a player must have. It does not say what the program runs.

## 2. Baylor offense, derived from PFF (2024 and 2025)

Source: `pff_premium` video plays. Baylor offense plays only. Shares are of all Baylor offense plays in the season.

| Item | 2024 (n = 1,153) | 2025 (n = 1,148) |
|---|---|---|
| Shotgun | 83% | 86% |
| Pistol | 0% | under 1% |
| Play action | 17% | 17% |
| No huddle | 0% | 0% |
| Pass plays (of run and pass calls) | 53% (500 of 948) | 61% (597 of 980) |
| Screen | 7% | 8% |
| Top personnel code | 3-0-1-1 (73%) | 3-0-1-1 (82%) |
| Top formations | 2x2, 3x1, 1x3 | 2x2, 3x1, 1x3 |
| Defense faced, most common | Nickel (64%) | Nickel (81%) |

Read: a shotgun, pass-leaning offense with one personnel grouping used most of the time. Run concepts are mostly blank in the feed. Coded run concepts that appear are split, cross lead and read option.

Gaps:
- Video plays exist only for 2024 and 2025 in the database. 2023 and 2026 are not covered by this read.
- Personnel codes are shown as PFF writes them. We have not confirmed the code key with PFF docs.

## 3. OC background and scheme lineage

Sources: Wikipedia, "Jake Spavital" (checked 2026-10-23), and Baylor Lariat, August 2024 (as given in the brief; not re-checked here).

Career (Wikipedia):
- 2008: Tulsa, offensive quality control under Gus Malzahn.
- 2009: Houston, graduate assistant under Kevin Sumlin and Dana Holgorsen.
- 2010: Oklahoma State, graduate assistant under Holgorsen. Brandon Weeden was third in the nation in yards per game and total yards.
- 2011 to 2012: West Virginia, quarterbacks coach under Holgorsen (Geno Smith).
- 2013 to 2015: Texas A&M, co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach (2013: Johnny Manziel). Offensive coordinator from 2014.
- 2016: California, offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach. Interim head coach in January 2017.
- 2017 to 2018: West Virginia, offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach under Holgorsen.
- 2019 to 2022: Texas State, head coach. Record 13 to 35.
- 2023: California, offensive coordinator under Justin Wilcox (rehired December 2022).
- 2024 to present: Baylor, offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach under Dave Aranda. Announced November 30, 2023.

Scheme lineage (inference, not confirmed by a source):
- The Holgorsen tree (Oklahoma State, West Virginia, Texas A&M) is the most likely base. Wikipedia says he took Holgorsen's offense to each stop. Neither source describes any stop's offense in detail.

Baylor change in 2024 (Baylor Lariat, August 2024, as given in the brief):
- Up-tempo spread, more downfield passing, fewer tight ends, receiver-driven.
- Spavital calls plays and coaches quarterbacks.
- Check against the PFF scheme read in section 2: shotgun about 85% and pass share 53% to 61% fit a spread, pass-leaning offense.

## 4. Requirements by position, with the PFF metric that can test each one

Only traits with a PFF link are listed. Other traits (for example size, toughness, speed) need film or measurement data, not PFF.

| Position | Scale traits (from the sheet) | PFF metric that can test it now | Not testable from PFF |
|---|---|---|---|
| OT | Edge protection, anchor, bend, foot speed | Pressure rate on pass-pro rows (proxy) | Size, toughness |
| OG and C | Anchor, pulling, second-level blocking | Pressure rate; run-block grade (reference) | Pulling, second-level blocking |
| WR and slot | Suddenness and route running, ball skills and hands, YAC | Target share; drops; yards after catch (pff_stats) | Separation grade, route depth |
| TE | Blocking, catch in traffic | Targets; run-block grade (reference) | Blocking grade is not in the profile yet |
| RB | Contact balance, YAC, cutting, vision | Runs per snap; yards after contact (pff_stats) | Vision, cutting |
| END and JACK | Pass rush, tackling, strength at point of attack | Pass rush per snap; tackles per snap | Tackling quality, strength |
| DT | Leverage, use of hands, pad level | Tackles per snap; pass rush per snap (DI, weak) | Leverage, hands |
| ILB | Tackling, range, pass rush | Tackles per snap; pass rush per snap | Range |
| CB and STAR | Man coverage, ball skills, tackling | Burns, targets against (defensive_targets) | Man coverage grade |
| SAF | Range, key and diagnose, run support | Tackles per snap; missed tackles | Range, keying |
| QB | Accuracy, decisions, escapability | QB charting: pass accuracy, throw type | Anticipation, timing (not charted here) |

## 4. How the scheme and requirements combine (planned, not built)

- Scheme fit: a player's profile by scheme cell (for example OL pressure in shotgun, WR share on passing downs), compared with the same cell for the FBS baseline.
- Programmatic fit: the situation-adjusted profile compared with the position requirement above (for example edge pass rush per snap against the END pass-rush trait).
- Each fit output carries its sample size and reliability. Use the rule: split-half at least 0.6 and year-to-year at least 0.4.

## 5. Step 1 test result (summary)

Script: `scripts/split_stability.py`. Output: `data/split_stability.csv`. Non-Baylor rows, 2023 to 2026.

- OL pressure, all rows: split-half 0.59, year-to-year 0.55. Verdict: use with shrinkage.
- OL pressure, shotgun: split-half 0.59, year-to-year 0.52. No gain over all rows. Under-center cell too small (3 player-seasons).
- OL pressure, passing down vs standard: split-half 0.65 and 0.62. Year-to-year cannot be computed (22 and 26 pairs, under the 40 needed).
- WR target share, shotgun: split-half 0.55, year-to-year 0.29. Verdict: use with shrinkage on split-half, but year-to-year is below 0.4.
- WR target share, passing down: split-half 0.30. Verdict: exclude. The standard cell is the complement, so its numbers match.

Conclusion: the shotgun and down-and-distance splits do not clear the rule. The data is too thin for year-to-year. Do not use these splits in published profiles yet.

## 6. Decisions (Eric, 2026-10-23)

1. Use the GRD SCALE thresholds as written. Done in section 4.
2. Accept time to pressure as the pressure proxy. Still a proxy, not the PFF pressure grade.
3. Pull the 2023 and 2026 video plays so the scheme read covers all four seasons. In progress; section 2 will be updated when done.

Only traits with a PFF link are listed. Other traits (for example size, toughness, speed) need film or measurement data, not PFF.

| Position | Scale traits (from the sheet) | PFF metric that can test it now | Not testable from PFF |
|---|---|---|---|
| OT | Edge protection, anchor, bend, foot speed | Pressure rate on pass-pro rows (proxy) | Size, toughness |
| OG and C | Anchor, pulling, second-level blocking | Pressure rate; run-block grade (reference) | Pulling, second-level blocking |
| WR and slot | Suddenness and route running, ball skills and hands, YAC | Target share; drops; yards after catch (pff_stats) | Separation grade, route depth |
| TE | Blocking, catch in traffic | Targets; run-block grade (reference) | Blocking grade is not in the profile yet |
| RB | Contact balance, YAC, cutting, vision | Runs per snap; yards after contact (pff_stats) | Vision, cutting |
| END and JACK | Pass rush, tackling, strength at point of attack | Pass rush per snap; tackles per snap | Tackling quality, strength |
| DT | Leverage, use of hands, pad level | Tackles per snap; pass rush per snap (DI, weak) | Leverage, hands |
| ILB | Tackling, range, pass rush | Tackles per snap; pass rush per snap | Range |
| CB and STAR | Man coverage, ball skills, tackling | Burns, targets against (defensive_targets) | Man coverage grade |
| SAF | Range, key and diagnose, run support | Tackles per snap; missed tackles | Range, keying |
| QB | Accuracy, decisions, escapability | QB charting: pass accuracy, throw type | Anticipation, timing (not charted here) |

## 4. How the scheme and requirements combine (planned, not built)

- Scheme fit: a player's profile by scheme cell (for example OL pressure in shotgun, WR share on passing downs), compared with the same cell for the FBS baseline.
- Programmatic fit: the situation-adjusted profile compared with the position requirement above (for example edge pass rush per snap against the END pass-rush trait).
- Each fit output carries its sample size and reliability. Use the rule: split-half at least 0.6 and year-to-year at least 0.4.

## 5. Step 1 test result (summary)

Script: `scripts/split_stability.py`. Output: `data/split_stability.csv`. Non-Baylor rows, 2023 to 2026.

- OL pressure, all rows: split-half 0.59, year-to-year 0.55. Verdict: use with shrinkage.
- OL pressure, shotgun: split-half 0.59, year-to-year 0.52. No gain over all rows. Under-center cell too small (3 player-seasons).
- OL pressure, passing down vs standard: split-half 0.65 and 0.62. Year-to-year cannot be computed (22 and 26 pairs, under the 40 needed).
- WR target share, shotgun: split-half 0.55, year-to-year 0.29. Verdict: use with shrinkage on split-half, but year-to-year is below 0.4.
- WR target share, passing down: split-half 0.30. Verdict: exclude. The standard cell is the complement, so its numbers match.

Conclusion: the shotgun and down-and-distance splits do not clear the rule. The data is too thin for year-to-year. Do not use these splits in published profiles yet.

## 6. Decisions (Eric, 2026-10-23)

1. Use the GRD SCALE thresholds as written. Done in section 4.
2. Accept time to pressure as the pressure proxy. Still a proxy, not the PFF pressure grade.
3. Pull the 2023 and 2026 video plays so the scheme read covers all four seasons. In progress; section 2 will be updated when done.

# STATUS

## Current state

- Draft PR #1 on branch `qb-fbs-baseline` holds all code for QB, O-line, LB, DB, RB, WR and the Power Four driver analysis.
- All models use the FBS baseline, count features only, with PFF grades as the outcome. Results are weak. No position has a usable predictor.
- Reports are in Drive `PFF_endpoint/reports/<position>/` (qb, oline, lb, db, rb, wr, drivers). Each is confirmed through the connector.

- Scheme and requirements draft is on Drive: `PFF_endpoint/athlete_profiles/scheme_requirements_draft.md`. It uses `PP_Recruiting / 000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` as the position-requirement source, and reads Baylor's 2024 and 2025 offense from PFF video plays (shotgun about 85%, one personnel grouping most of the time).
- Step 1 split test (`scripts/split_stability.py`, output `data/split_stability.csv`): shotgun and down-and-distance splits do not clear the reliability rule. OL pressure is 0.59 split-half in shotgun, same as all rows. Passing-down year-to-year has too few pairs.

## Next

1. Decide whether to build WR receptions and yards-after-catch features, now that a receiver id is confirmed.
2. Decide whether to re-pull the charting feed with the video-play receiver field, after its id type is checked.
3. Review draft PR #1 before any merge.
4. Pull 2023 and 2026 video plays so the scheme read covers all four seasons.

## Open questions

- Outcome for the next round: keep PFF grade per game, or switch to EPA or a coach-rated outcome?
- Receiver id in the video plays feed (`pass_receiver_target`): not matched to roster ids yet. Id type unknown.
- Whether to add opponent strength to WR, LB, DB and RB (done for QB only).
- Which GRD SCALE traits can be tested from PFF, and whether to re-weight the eight factors to them.
- Pressure proxy (`time_to_pressure` set) is not the PFF pressure grade. Accept the proxy, or find a true pressure flag?

## Gotchas

- Receiver link: premium passing `target_player_id` matches a WR grade row in the same game for only about 48% to 56% of target ids. The rest are TEs, RBs or others.
- Field roles are unverified against the PFF docs: `tackler_player_id`, `pass_rush` `player_id`, `runner_player_id`, `target_player_id`, and the premium `all_blocking` and `pressure` ids.
- The 2023 WR pull had 2 failed game calls (426 of 428 read). Not re-pulled.
- Scratch venv and probe scripts live outside the repo (in the session scratchpad). Only pull and model scripts are committed.
- Git: an automatic session-end commit (not from the user) added two scripts earlier. Its message is generic.

"""Read-only pull of premium passing target ids for FBS games, one season per run.

Per game: passing rows, rows with a target_player_id, and targets per receiver id. Totals only.
Writes data/wr_<season>.json. The WR link is made later through the game grade rows (position WR).
"""
import sys, os, json, time, collections
sys.path.insert(0, os.environ.get("PFF_PIPELINE_DIR", "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Football/PFF_Data_Project"))
from dotenv import load_dotenv

OUT = os.environ.get("PFF_WORK_DIR", "data")
SEASON = int(os.environ["PFF_SEASON"])
WEEKS = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}
c = PFFClient()
def rows_of(p):
    if isinstance(p, list): return p

fbs = {str(x.get("franchise_id")) for x in t if any(g.get("name") == "FBS" for g in (x.get("groups") or []))}
games = c.get_games(SEASON); g = games if isinstance(games, list) else games.get("games", [])
sel = [x for x in g if x.get("week") in WEEKS and (str(x.get("home_franchise_id")) in fbs or str(x.get("away_franchise_id")) in fbs)]
games_out, targets, fails = [], collections.Counter(), []
t0 = time.time()
for i, x in enumerate(sel, 1):
    gid, wk = str(x["id"]), int(x["week"])
    try:
        rows = rows_of(c.get_premium_game(gid, "passing"))
        n_rows = len(rows); n_tgt = 0
        for r in rows:
            tid = r.get("target_player_id")
            if tid not in (None, ""):
                n_tgt += 1; targets[(gid, str(tid))] += 1
        games_out.append({"game_id": gid, "week": wk, "passing_rows": n_rows, "rows_with_target": n_tgt})
    except Exception as e:
        fails.append((gid, type(e).__name__, getattr(getattr(e, "response", None), "status_code", None)))
    if i % 100 == 0:
        print(f"{i}/{len(sel)} {time.time()-t0:.0f}s fails={len(fails)}", flush=True)
json.dump({"season": SEASON, "games": games_out, "targets": [{"game_id": k[0], "player_id": k[1], "n_targets": v} for k, v in targets.items()], "fails": fails},
          open(os.path.join(OUT, f"wr_{SEASON}.json"), "w"))
print("DONE season", SEASON, "games", len(sel), "fails", len(fails), flush=True)
