"""WR on the FBS baseline: targets per snap (count only), multi-season, rolling 4-game windows, no grade features.

Outcome: PFF offense grade per WR per game. WR rows and snaps: data/oline_pull*.json (all positions).
Targets: data/wr_<season>.json (premium passing target_player_id). A target links to a WR when the same id is a
WR grade row in the same game. Link rate is reported. Field role is unverified against the PFF docs.
Before = 2026 weeks 1-4 only. After = all seasons pooled. Test: 2026 weeks 5 and 7, non-Baylor.
"""
import os, json, glob, warnings
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNetCV, ElasticNet
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
W = os.environ.get("PFF_WORK_DIR", "data")
WEEKS = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}
FEAT = ["targets_per_snap", "snaps"]

def season(s):
    gp = os.path.join(W, "oline_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"oline_pull_{s}.json")
    fp = os.path.join(W, "fbs_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"fbs_pull_{s}.json")
    wp = os.path.join(W, f"wr_{s}.json")
    if not all(os.path.exists(x) for x in [gp, fp, wp]):
        return None, None
    fbs = set(json.load(open(fp))["fbs_franchises"])
    g = pd.DataFrame(json.load(open(gp))["grades"])
    g["team_id"] = g["team_id"].astype(str); g["player_id"] = g["player_id"].astype(str)
    g = g[g["team_id"].isin(fbs)].drop_duplicates(["game_id", "player_id"])
    g = g[g["week"].isin(WEEKS)]
    wr = g[g["position"] == "WR"].copy()
    wr["season"] = s; wr["week"] = wr["week"].astype(int)
    wr["snaps"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["snaps"], errors="coerce"); wr["offense"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["offense"], errors="coerce")
    wr["baylor"] = wr["team_id"] == "118"
    w = json.load(open(wp))
    tg = pd.DataFrame(w["targets"])
    tg["player_id"] = tg["player_id"].astype(str)
    # link check: each target id should be a WR grade row in the same game
    wr_keys = set(zip(wr["game_id"], wr["player_id"]))
    tg["is_wr"] = [ (gid, pid) in wr_keys for gid, pid in zip(tg["game_id"], tg["player_id"]) ]
    link = {"season": s, "target_ids": len(tg), "linked_to_wr": int(tg["is_wr"].sum()), "games": len(w["games"]),
            "games_with_target_field": int(sum(1 for x in w["games"] if x["rows_with_target"] > 0)),
            "passing_rows": int(sum(x["passing_rows"] for x in w["games"])), "rows_with_target": int(sum(x["rows_with_target"] for x in w["games"]))}
    tg = tg[tg["is_wr"]][["game_id", "player_id", "n_targets"]]
    wr = wr.merge(tg, on=["game_id", "player_id"], how="left")
    wr["n_targets"] = wr["n_targets"].fillna(0)
    wr["targets_per_snap"] = wr["n_targets"] / wr["snaps"].replace(0, np.nan)
    return wr, link

frames, links = [], []
for s in range(2018, 2027):
    f, l = season(s)
    if f is not None:
        frames.append(f); links.append(l)
pd.DataFrame(links).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_link_rates.csv"), index=False)
print(pd.DataFrame(links).to_string(index=False))
allw = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
allw = allw[(allw.snaps > 0) & allw.offense.notna()].dropna(subset=FEAT).copy()
print("WR player-games:", len(allw), "baylor:", int(allw.baylor.sum()), "players:", allw[~allw.baylor].player_id.nunique())
allw = allw.sort_values(["season", "player_id", "week"])
for col in FEAT + ["offense"]:
    allw[f"roll4_{col}"] = allw.groupby(["season", "player_id"])[col].transform(lambda s_: s_.rolling(4, min_periods=2).mean())
ROLLF = [f"roll4_{f}" for f in FEAT]
test_m = lambda d: (d.season == 2026) & d.week.isin([5, 7]) & (~d.baylor)
trn_m = lambda d: (~d.baylor) & ((d.season < 2026) | ((d.season == 2026) & (d.week <= 4)))

def fit_en(X, y, groups):
    return ElasticNetCV(l1_ratio=[0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0], alphas=np.logspace(-3, 1, 30),
                        cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=4).split(X, y, groups), max_iter=20000).fit(X, y)

def score(feats, target, label, pool):
    d = allw.dropna(subset=feats + [target]); tr = d[trn_m(d) & pool(d)]; te = d[test_m(d)]
    if len(tr) < 30 or len(te) < 5:
        print(label, "too few", len(tr), len(te)); return None
    mu, sd = tr[feats].mean(), tr[feats].std().replace(0, 1)
    Z = lambda x: ((x[feats] - mu) / sd).values
    en = fit_en(Z(tr), tr[target].values, tr.game_id.values)
    r2 = r2_score(te[target], en.predict(Z(te)))
    print(f"{label}: test R2={r2:.3f} train n={len(tr)} test n={len(te)}", flush=True)
    return r2, len(tr), len(te), en, mu, sd, Z, d

rows = []
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "BEFORE: 2026 weeks 1-4 only", lambda d: d.season == 2026)
if r: rows.append(("before: 2026 weeks 1-4, single-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "AFTER A: all seasons pooled, single-game", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r: rows.append(("after A: all seasons, single-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
r = score(ROLLF, "roll4_offense", "AFTER B: all seasons, rolling 4-game", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r: rows.append(("after B: all seasons, rolling 4-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", "test_R2", "n_train", "n_test"]).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_results.csv"), index=False)
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "coefficients (pooled single-game)", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r:
    _, _, _, en, mu, sd, Z, d = r
    tr_all = d[~d.baylor]; games = tr_all.game_id.unique(); rng = np.random.default_rng(11); B = []
    for _ in range(200):
        pk = rng.choice(games, len(games), replace=True)
        bs = pd.concat([tr_all[tr_all.game_id == gg] for gg in pk])
        B.append(ElasticNet(alpha=en.alpha_, l1_ratio=en.l1_ratio_, max_iter=20000).fit(((bs[FEAT] - mu) / sd).values, bs["offense"].values).coef_)
    B = np.array(B)
    for i, f in enumerate(FEAT):
        print(f"   {f:18s} coef={en.coef_[i]:+.3f} CI [{np.percentile(B[:, i], 2.5):+.3f}, {np.percentile(B[:, i], 97.5):+.3f}]")
    by = d[d.baylor].copy(); by["pred"] = en.predict(Z(by)); by["resid"] = by["offense"] - by["pred"]
    print(f"Baylor WR player-games n={len(by)}: mean residual={by.resid.mean():+.2f}")
    bg = by.game_id.unique(); bb = []
    for _ in range(1000):
        pk = rng.choice(bg, len(bg), replace=True); bb.append(by[by.game_id.isin(pk)].resid.mean())
    print(f"   bootstrap 95% CI [{np.percentile(bb, 2.5):+.2f}, {np.percentile(bb, 97.5):+.2f}]")
    by[["season", "week", "game_id", "team_id", "player_id", "snaps", "n_targets", "offense", "pred", "resid"]].round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_baylor_scored.csv"), index=False)
    allw[["season", "week", "game_id", "team_id", "player_id", "snaps", "n_targets", "targets_per_snap", "offense", "baylor"]].to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_player_game.csv"), index=False)

"""WR on the FBS baseline: targets per snap (count only), multi-season, rolling 4-game windows, no grade features.

Outcome: PFF offense grade per WR per game. WR rows and snaps: data/oline_pull*.json (all positions).
Targets: data/wr_<season>.json (premium passing target_player_id). A target links to a WR when the same id is a
WR grade row in the same game. Link rate is reported. Field role is unverified against the PFF docs.
Before = 2026 weeks 1-4 only. After = all seasons pooled. Test: 2026 weeks 5 and 7, non-Baylor.
"""
import os, json, glob, warnings
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNetCV, ElasticNet
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
W = os.environ.get("PFF_WORK_DIR", "data")
WEEKS = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}
FEAT = ["targets_per_snap", "snaps"]

def season_db_targets(s, g, tp, wp):
    """2023 to 2026 path. Targets are WR-coded in the feed (data/wr_targets_<s>.csv, from the DB). A WR-coded
    receiver links to any grade row in the same game, because about a quarter are graded as TE or HB.
    Those rows join the WR pool with role "target_link" so their snaps and offense count.
    shortcut: a TE or HB grade counts as a WR for the games it is a WR-coded target; upgrade when receiver snaps load.
    """
    tg = pd.read_csv(tp, dtype={"player_id": str})
    key = lambda df: pd.MultiIndex.from_frame(df[["game_id", "player_id"]])
    any_grade = key(tg).isin(key(g))
    wr_grade = key(tg).isin(key(g[g["position"] == "WR"]))
    link = {"season": s, "target_ids": len(tg), "linked_to_wr": int(any_grade.sum()),
            "linked_to_wr_grade": int(wr_grade.sum()), "source": "db_wr_coded"}
    keep = tg[any_grade][["game_id", "player_id", "n_targets"]]
    wr = g[(g["position"] == "WR") | key(g).isin(key(keep))].copy()
    wr["role"] = np.where(wr["position"] == "WR", "WR grade", "target_link")
    wr["season"] = s; wr["week"] = wr["week"].astype(int)
    wr["snaps"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["snaps"], errors="coerce"); wr["offense"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["offense"], errors="coerce")
    wr["baylor"] = wr["team_id"] == "118"
    wr = wr.merge(keep, on=["game_id", "player_id"], how="left")
    wr["n_targets"] = wr["n_targets"].fillna(0)
    wr["targets_per_snap"] = wr["n_targets"] / wr["snaps"].replace(0, np.nan)
    return wr, link

def season(s):
    gp = os.path.join(W, "oline_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"oline_pull_{s}.json")
    fp = os.path.join(W, "fbs_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"fbs_pull_{s}.json")
    wp = os.path.join(W, f"wr_{s}.json")
    if not all(os.path.exists(x) for x in [gp, fp, wp]):
        return None, None
    fbs = set(json.load(open(fp))["fbs_franchises"])
    g = pd.DataFrame(json.load(open(gp))["grades"])
    g["team_id"] = g["team_id"].astype(str); g["player_id"] = g["player_id"].astype(str)
    g = g[g["team_id"].isin(fbs)].drop_duplicates(["game_id", "player_id"])
    g = g[g["week"].isin(WEEKS)]
    tp = os.path.join(W, f"wr_targets_{s}.csv")
    if os.path.exists(tp):
        return season_db_targets(s, g, tp, wp)
    wr = g[g["position"] == "WR"].copy()
    wr["season"] = s; wr["week"] = wr["week"].astype(int)
    wr["snaps"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["snaps"], errors="coerce"); wr["offense"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["offense"], errors="coerce")
    wr["baylor"] = wr["team_id"] == "118"
    w = json.load(open(wp))
    tg = pd.DataFrame(w["targets"])
    tg["player_id"] = tg["player_id"].astype(str)
    # link check: each target id should be a WR grade row in the same game
    wr_keys = set(zip(wr["game_id"], wr["player_id"]))
    tg["is_wr"] = [ (gid, pid) in wr_keys for gid, pid in zip(tg["game_id"], tg["player_id"]) ]
    link = {"season": s, "target_ids": len(tg), "linked_to_wr": int(tg["is_wr"].sum()), "games": len(w["games"]),
            "games_with_target_field": int(sum(1 for x in w["games"] if x["rows_with_target"] > 0)),
            "passing_rows": int(sum(x["passing_rows"] for x in w["games"])), "rows_with_target": int(sum(x["rows_with_target"] for x in w["games"]))}
    tg = tg[tg["is_wr"]][["game_id", "player_id", "n_targets"]]
    wr = wr.merge(tg, on=["game_id", "player_id"], how="left")
    wr["n_targets"] = wr["n_targets"].fillna(0)
    wr["targets_per_snap"] = wr["n_targets"] / wr["snaps"].replace(0, np.nan)
    return wr, link

frames, links = [], []
for s in range(2018, 2027):
    f, l = season(s)
    if f is not None:
        frames.append(f); links.append(l)
pd.DataFrame(links).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_link_rates.csv"), index=False)
print(pd.DataFrame(links).to_string(index=False))
allw = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
allw = allw[(allw.snaps > 0) & allw.offense.notna()].dropna(subset=FEAT).copy()
print("WR player-games:", len(allw), "baylor:", int(allw.baylor.sum()), "players:", allw[~allw.baylor].player_id.nunique())
allw = allw.sort_values(["season", "player_id", "week"])
for col in FEAT + ["offense"]:
    allw[f"roll4_{col}"] = allw.groupby(["season", "player_id"])[col].transform(lambda s_: s_.rolling(4, min_periods=2).mean())
ROLLF = [f"roll4_{f}" for f in FEAT]
test_m = lambda d: (d.season == 2026) & d.week.isin([5, 7]) & (~d.baylor)
trn_m = lambda d: (~d.baylor) & ((d.season < 2026) | ((d.season == 2026) & (d.week <= 4)))

def fit_en(X, y, groups):
    return ElasticNetCV(l1_ratio=[0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0], alphas=np.logspace(-3, 1, 30),
                        cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=4).split(X, y, groups), max_iter=20000).fit(X, y)

def score(feats, target, label, pool):
    d = allw.dropna(subset=feats + [target]); tr = d[trn_m(d) & pool(d)]; te = d[test_m(d)]
    if len(tr) < 30 or len(te) < 5:
        print(label, "too few", len(tr), len(te)); return None
    mu, sd = tr[feats].mean(), tr[feats].std().replace(0, 1)
    Z = lambda x: ((x[feats] - mu) / sd).values
    en = fit_en(Z(tr), tr[target].values, tr.game_id.values)
    r2 = r2_score(te[target], en.predict(Z(te)))
    print(f"{label}: test R2={r2:.3f} train n={len(tr)} test n={len(te)}", flush=True)
    return r2, len(tr), len(te), en, mu, sd, Z, d

rows = []
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "BEFORE: 2026 weeks 1-4 only", lambda d: d.season == 2026)
if r: rows.append(("before: 2026 weeks 1-4, single-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "AFTER A: all seasons pooled, single-game", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r: rows.append(("after A: all seasons, single-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
r = score(ROLLF, "roll4_offense", "AFTER B: all seasons, rolling 4-game", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r: rows.append(("after B: all seasons, rolling 4-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", "test_R2", "n_train", "n_test"]).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_results.csv"), index=False)

"""WR on the FBS baseline: targets per snap (count only), multi-season, rolling 4-game windows, no grade features.

Outcome: PFF offense grade per WR per game. WR rows and snaps: data/oline_pull*.json (all positions).
Targets: data/wr_<season>.json (premium passing target_player_id). A target links to a WR when the same id is a
WR grade row in the same game. Link rate is reported. Field role is unverified against the PFF docs.
Before = 2026 weeks 1-4 only. After = all seasons pooled. Test: 2026 weeks 5 and 7, non-Baylor.
"""
import os, json, glob, warnings
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNetCV, ElasticNet
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
W = os.environ.get("PFF_WORK_DIR", "data")
WEEKS = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}
FEAT = ["targets_per_snap", "snaps"]

def season_db_targets(s, g, tp, wp):
    """2023 to 2026 path. Targets are WR-coded in the feed (data/wr_targets_<s>.csv, from the DB). A WR-coded
    receiver links to any grade row in the same game, because about a quarter are graded as TE or HB.
    Those rows join the WR pool with role "target_link" so their snaps and offense count.
    shortcut: a TE or HB grade counts as a WR for the games it is a WR-coded target; upgrade when receiver snaps load.
    """
    tg = pd.read_csv(tp, dtype={"game_id": str, "player_id": str})
    key = lambda df: pd.MultiIndex.from_frame(df[["game_id", "player_id"]])
    any_grade = key(tg).isin(key(g))
    wr_grade = key(tg).isin(key(g[g["position"] == "WR"]))
    link = {"season": s, "target_ids": len(tg), "linked_to_wr": int(any_grade.sum()),
            "linked_to_wr_grade": int(wr_grade.sum()), "source": "db_wr_coded"}
    keep = tg[any_grade][["game_id", "player_id", "n_targets"]]
    wr = g[(g["position"] == "WR") | key(g).isin(key(keep))].copy()
    wr["role"] = np.where(wr["position"] == "WR", "WR grade", "target_link")
    wr["season"] = s; wr["week"] = wr["week"].astype(int)
    wr["snaps"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["snaps"], errors="coerce"); wr["offense"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["offense"], errors="coerce")
    wr["baylor"] = wr["team_id"] == "118"
    wr = wr.merge(keep, on=["game_id", "player_id"], how="left")
    wr["n_targets"] = wr["n_targets"].fillna(0)
    wr["targets_per_snap"] = wr["n_targets"] / wr["snaps"].replace(0, np.nan)
    return wr, link

def season(s):
    gp = os.path.join(W, "oline_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"oline_pull_{s}.json")
    fp = os.path.join(W, "fbs_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"fbs_pull_{s}.json")
    wp = os.path.join(W, f"wr_{s}.json")
    if not all(os.path.exists(x) for x in [gp, fp, wp]):
        return None, None
    fbs = set(json.load(open(fp))["fbs_franchises"])
    g = pd.DataFrame(json.load(open(gp))["grades"])
    g["team_id"] = g["team_id"].astype(str); g["player_id"] = g["player_id"].astype(str)
    g = g[g["team_id"].isin(fbs)].drop_duplicates(["game_id", "player_id"])
    g = g[g["week"].isin(WEEKS)]
    tp = os.path.join(W, f"wr_targets_{s}.csv")
    if os.path.exists(tp):
        return season_db_targets(s, g, tp, wp)
    wr = g[g["position"] == "WR"].copy()
    wr["season"] = s; wr["week"] = wr["week"].astype(int)
    wr["snaps"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["snaps"], errors="coerce"); wr["offense"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["offense"], errors="coerce")
    wr["baylor"] = wr["team_id"] == "118"
    w = json.load(open(wp))
    tg = pd.DataFrame(w["targets"])
    tg["player_id"] = tg["player_id"].astype(str)
    # link check: each target id should be a WR grade row in the same game
    wr_keys = set(zip(wr["game_id"], wr["player_id"]))
    tg["is_wr"] = [ (gid, pid) in wr_keys for gid, pid in zip(tg["game_id"], tg["player_id"]) ]
    link = {"season": s, "target_ids": len(tg), "linked_to_wr": int(tg["is_wr"].sum()), "games": len(w["games"]),
            "games_with_target_field": int(sum(1 for x in w["games"] if x["rows_with_target"] > 0)),
            "passing_rows": int(sum(x["passing_rows"] for x in w["games"])), "rows_with_target": int(sum(x["rows_with_target"] for x in w["games"]))}
    tg = tg[tg["is_wr"]][["game_id", "player_id", "n_targets"]]
    wr = wr.merge(tg, on=["game_id", "player_id"], how="left")
    wr["n_targets"] = wr["n_targets"].fillna(0)
    wr["targets_per_snap"] = wr["n_targets"] / wr["snaps"].replace(0, np.nan)
    return wr, link

frames, links = [], []
for s in range(2018, 2027):
    f, l = season(s)
    if f is not None:
        frames.append(f); links.append(l)
pd.DataFrame(links).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_link_rates.csv"), index=False)
print(pd.DataFrame(links).to_string(index=False))
allw = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
allw = allw[(allw.snaps > 0) & allw.offense.notna()].dropna(subset=FEAT).copy()
print("WR player-games:", len(allw), "baylor:", int(allw.baylor.sum()), "players:", allw[~allw.baylor].player_id.nunique())
allw = allw.sort_values(["season", "player_id", "week"])
for col in FEAT + ["offense"]:
    allw[f"roll4_{col}"] = allw.groupby(["season", "player_id"])[col].transform(lambda s_: s_.rolling(4, min_periods=2).mean())
ROLLF = [f"roll4_{f}" for f in FEAT]
test_m = lambda d: (d.season == 2026) & d.week.isin([5, 7]) & (~d.baylor)
trn_m = lambda d: (~d.baylor) & ((d.season < 2026) | ((d.season == 2026) & (d.week <= 4)))

def fit_en(X, y, groups):
    return ElasticNetCV(l1_ratio=[0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0], alphas=np.logspace(-3, 1, 30),
                        cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=4).split(X, y, groups), max_iter=20000).fit(X, y)

def score(feats, target, label, pool):
    d = allw.dropna(subset=feats + [target]); tr = d[trn_m(d) & pool(d)]; te = d[test_m(d)]
    if len(tr) < 30 or len(te) < 5:
        print(label, "too few", len(tr), len(te)); return None
    mu, sd = tr[feats].mean(), tr[feats].std().replace(0, 1)
    Z = lambda x: ((x[feats] - mu) / sd).values
    en = fit_en(Z(tr), tr[target].values, tr.game_id.values)
    r2 = r2_score(te[target], en.predict(Z(te)))
    print(f"{label}: test R2={r2:.3f} train n={len(tr)} test n={len(te)}", flush=True)
    return r2, len(tr), len(te), en, mu, sd, Z, d

rows = []
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "BEFORE: 2026 weeks 1-4 only", lambda d: d.season == 2026)
if r: rows.append(("before: 2026 weeks 1-4, single-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "AFTER A: all seasons pooled, single-game", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r: rows.append(("after A: all seasons, single-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
r = score(ROLLF, "roll4_offense", "AFTER B: all seasons, rolling 4-game", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r: rows.append(("after B: all seasons, rolling 4-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", "test_R2", "n_train", "n_test"]).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_results.csv"), index=False)
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "coefficients (pooled single-game)", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r:
    _, _, _, en, mu, sd, Z, d = r
    tr_all = d[~d.baylor]; games = tr_all.game_id.unique(); rng = np.random.default_rng(11); B = []
    for _ in range(200):
        pk = rng.choice(games, len(games), replace=True)
        bs = pd.concat([tr_all[tr_all.game_id == gg] for gg in pk])
        B.append(ElasticNet(alpha=en.alpha_, l1_ratio=en.l1_ratio_, max_iter=20000).fit(((bs[FEAT] - mu) / sd).values, bs["offense"].values).coef_)
    B = np.array(B)
    for i, f in enumerate(FEAT):
        print(f"   {f:18s} coef={en.coef_[i]:+.3f} CI [{np.percentile(B[:, i], 2.5):+.3f}, {np.percentile(B[:, i], 97.5):+.3f}]")
    by = d[d.baylor].copy(); by["pred"] = en.predict(Z(by)); by["resid"] = by["offense"] - by["pred"]
    print(f"Baylor WR player-games n={len(by)}: mean residual={by.resid.mean():+.2f}")
    bg = by.game_id.unique(); bb = []
    for _ in range(1000):
        pk = rng.choice(bg, len(bg), replace=True); bb.append(by[by.game_id.isin(pk)].resid.mean())
    print(f"   bootstrap 95% CI [{np.percentile(bb, 2.5):+.2f}, {np.percentile(bb, 97.5):+.2f}]")
    by[["season", "week", "game_id", "team_id", "player_id", "snaps", "n_targets", "offense", "pred", "resid"]].round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_baylor_scored.csv"), index=False)
    allw[["season", "week", "game_id", "team_id", "player_id", "snaps", "n_targets", "targets_per_snap", "offense", "baylor"]].to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_player_game.csv"), index=False)

Looking at the link-within-weeks results by year, they're around 84-87% for 2023-2025 but drop to 74% for 2026, while the old method's ~51% isn't directly comparable since its denominators included all target ids. I notice the target count dropped sharply from 62,639 to 9,598, which looks like a regression since the previous counts included all target rows, not just WR ones.

Checking the magnitude: roughly 7,500 target IDs per season with average n_targets around 1.5 gives about 11k per season, so across four seasons that lands near 45-62k, which matches the earlier total — meaning the old merge likely linked all target rows tied to WR-graded players across multiple seasons, not just a single week's targets. Even stranger, the DB's full-season pair count for 2023 across all weeks is 2190 — still less than the old season's 3828 — which tells me the old JSON targets data isn't drawn from the same pairing logic as the DB, since it's producing more matched pairs than even the DB's unrestricted total allows.

The source of the mismatch is likely that the old pull's targets dict was keyed by game/player ID and counted rows from the premium passing API endpoint directly, while the DB's premium passing table may only contain a partial subset of those rows due to failed or incomplete pulls. I'm trying to verify this by comparing passing row totals between the two sources — the API-based count was 32,288 passing rows for 2023, and I need to check what the DB shows for passing rows in that same season and week range, since I already know the DB's pass-protection table has 62,274 rows across 128 games for 2023. This is a real discrepancy I should flag rather than paper over, since the WR target totals could be off by close to a factor of six depending on which source is right.

input.content:
"""Read-only re-pull of premium passing target rows with each target's position, FBS games, one season per run.

Same games and weeks as scripts/pull_wr.py. Per game and receiver: counts of targets by target_play_position
(for example RWR, SLWR, HB-L, TE-R). Writes data/wr_targets_<season>.json. Counts only, no raw rows.
"""
import sys, os, json, time, collections
sys.path.insert(0, os.environ.get("PFF_PIPELINE_DIR", "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Football/PFF_Data_Project"))
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv(os.path.join(os.environ.get("PFF_PIPELINE_DIR", "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Football/PFF_Data_Project"), ".env"))
from src.ingest.pff_client import PFFClient
OUT = os.environ.get("PFF_WORK_DIR", "data")
SEASON = int(os.environ["PFF_SEASON"])
WEEKS = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}
c = PFFClient()
def rows_of(p):
    if isinstance(p, list): return p
    return next((v for v in p.values() if isinstance(v, list)), []) if isinstance(p, dict) else []
teams = c.get_teams(SEASON); t = teams if isinstance(teams, list) else teams.get("teams", [])
fbs = {str(x.get("franchise_id")) for x in t if any(g.get("name") == "FBS" for g in (x.get("groups") or []))}
games = c.get_games(SEASON); g = games if isinstance(games, list) else games.get("games", [])
sel = [x for x in g if x.get("week") in WEEKS and (str(x.get("home_franchise_id")) in fbs or str(x.get("away_franchise_id")) in fbs)]
targets, games_out, fails = collections.Counter(), [], []
t0 = time.time()
for i, x in enumerate(sel, 1):
    gid, wk = str(x["id"]), int(x["week"])
    try:
        rows = rows_of(c.get_premium_game(gid, "passing"))
        n_tgt = 0
        for r in rows:
            tid = r.get("target_player_id")
            if tid in (None, ""):
                continue
            n_tgt += 1
            targets[(gid, wk, str(tid), str(r.get("target_play_position") or "blank"))] += 1
        games_out.append({"game_id": gid, "week": wk, "passing_rows": len(rows), "rows_with_target": n_tgt})
    except Exception as e:
        fails.append((gid, type(e).__name__, getattr(getattr(e, "response", None), "status_code", None)))
    if i % 100 == 0:

    keep = t.groupby(["game_id", "player_id"], as_index=False)["n_targets"].sum()
    key = lambda df: pd.MultiIndex.from_frame(df[["game_id", "player_id"]])
    any_grade = key(keep).isin(key(g))

    link = {"season": s, "target_ids": len(keep), "linked_to_wr": int(any_grade.sum()),
            "linked_to_wr_grade": int(wr_grade.sum()), "source": "api_position"}
    keep = keep[any_grade]
    wr = g[(g["position"] == "WR") | key(g).isin(key(keep))].copy()
    wr["role"] = np.where(wr["position"] == "WR", "WR grade", "target_link")
    wr["season"] = s; wr["week"] = wr["week"].astype(int)
    wr["snaps"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["snaps"], errors="coerce"); wr["offense"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["offense"], errors="coerce")
    wr["baylor"] = wr["team_id"] == "118"
    wr = wr.merge(keep, on=["game_id", "player_id"], how="left")
    wr["n_targets"] = wr["n_targets"].fillna(0)
    wr["targets_per_snap"] = wr["n_targets"] / wr["snaps"].replace(0, np.nan)
    return wr, link

def season(s):
    gp = os.path.join(W, "oline_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"oline_pull_{s}.json")
    fp = os.path.join(W, "fbs_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"fbs_pull_{s}.json")
    wp = os.path.join(W, f"wr_{s}.json")
    if not all(os.path.exists(x) for x in [gp, fp, wp]):
        return None, None
    fbs = set(json.load(open(fp))["fbs_franchises"])
    g = pd.DataFrame(json.load(open(gp))["grades"])
    g["team_id"] = g["team_id"].astype(str); g["player_id"] = g["player_id"].astype(str)
    g = g[g["team_id"].isin(fbs)].drop_duplicates(["game_id", "player_id"])
    g = g[g["week"].isin(WEEKS)]
    wr = g[g["position"] == "WR"].copy()
    wr["season"] = s; wr["week"] = wr["week"].astype(int)
    wr["snaps"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["snaps"], errors="coerce"); wr["offense"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["offense"], errors="coerce")
    wr["baylor"] = wr["team_id"] == "118"
    w = json.load(open(wp))
    tg = pd.DataFrame(w["targets"])
    tg["player_id"] = tg["player_id"].astype(str)

    wr_keys = set(zip(wr["game_id"], wr["player_id"]))
    tg["is_wr"] = [ (gid, pid) in wr_keys for gid, pid in zip(tg["game_id"], tg["player_id"]) ]
    link = {"season": s, "target_ids": len(tg), "linked_to_wr": int(tg["is_wr"].sum()), "games": len(w["games"]),

            "passing_rows": int(sum(x["passing_rows"] for x in w["games"])), "rows_with_target": int(sum(x["rows_with_target"] for x in w["games"]))}
    tg = tg[tg["is_wr"]][["game_id", "player_id", "n_targets"]]
    wr = wr.merge(tg, on=["game_id", "player_id"], how="left")
    wr["n_targets"] = wr["n_targets"].fillna(0)
    wr["targets_per_snap"] = wr["n_targets"] / wr["snaps"].replace(0, np.nan)
    return wr, link

def fit_en(X, y, groups):
    return ElasticNetCV(l1_ratio=[0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0], alphas=np.logspace(-3, 1, 30),
                        cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=4).split(X, y, groups), max_iter=20000).fit(X, y)

    d = allw.dropna(subset=feats + [target]); tr = d[trn_m(d) & pool(d)]; te = d[test_m(d)]
    if len(tr) < 30 or len(te) < 5:
        print(label, "too few", len(tr), len(te)); return None
    mu, sd = tr[feats].mean(), tr[feats].std().replace(0, 1)
    Z = lambda x: ((x[feats] - mu) / sd).values
    en = fit_en(Z(tr), tr[target].values, tr.game_id.values)
    r2 = r2_score(te[target], en.predict(Z(te)))
    print(f"{label}: test R2={r2:.3f} train n={len(tr)} test n={len(te)}", flush=True)

pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", "test_R2", "n_train", "n_test"]).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_results.csv"), index=False)

# ~/DEV — workspace map

Eric Rash — Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics. Sport science and
football analytics, plus the agent system that runs them.

This file is a **map, not a rulebook**. Behavior rules live in
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read only the index you need.

## Areas

| Area | Index | What lives there |
|---|---|---|
| Football | `FOOTBALL.md` | Game film, player analytics, CFB prediction. ~39k files — about two thirds of DEV. |
| Performance | `PERFORMANCE.md` | Athlete monitoring, testing, load, risk. GPS, force plate, VALD, DEXA, S2. |
| Research | `RESEARCH.md` | Literature, Zotero, book library, reading pipelines. |
| Platform | `PLATFORM.md` | KeystoneOS, dashboards, CLIs, scheduled jobs. |
| Program | `PROGRAM.md` | Staff reporting, curriculum, proposals, vetting, brand. |
| Personal | `PERSONAL.md` | Side projects. Not Baylor work. |
| Commands | `COMMANDS.md` | Desk reference: every report/project command Eric can run himself. |
| Workflow | `WORKFLOW.md` | The ideal day, week and semester: which skill, mod and ritual, when and why. |

## Elsewhere on disk

`~/DEV` in this file means the workspace root on the Mac. Machine paths are in `~/.claude/machine.md`.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/` | Parked projects. Not a git repo, so the consolidation sweep skips it. Has its own `README.md`. |
| `~/DEV/_INBOX/` | Loose files from the `~/DEV` root. Own repo. |
| SecondBrain vault | Obsidian vault, ~850 notes. Own `CLAUDE.md`. `~/SecondBrain`. |
| `~/.claude/skills/` | ~45 skills (plugins add more) |
| `~/go/bin/` | ~8 custom CLIs built with `cli-printing-press` |
| `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/knowledge/` | ~190 compiled articles |

## Cloud sessions

A cloud session (`CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`) has only this repo cloned. No
project folders, no `~/.claude`, no Drive mount. Work this way instead:

- **Open a project by attaching its repo.** The GitHub repo name is the folder
  name in the area index (`Football/PFF_Data_Project/` → `erash11/PFF_Data_Project`).
  Exceptions: `Website/` → `erash11/AppliedPerformance-Site`; `DexaProject/` has no
  repo and is never opened from the cloud. Not in the map? List Eric's repos and
  ask which one before guessing.
- **Then follow that repo's Session routine** (read `docs/STATUS.md` first; commit
  and push at the end). Nothing pushed means nothing the other machine can see.
- **Documents:** use the Google Drive connector. The mount paths in this file are
  Mac only.
- **Skip what only exists on a machine:** `recall.py`, `memsearch`, Tier A memory files,
  SecondBrain, `~/go/bin` CLIs, local databases (DuckDB, `.rds`). If a task
  needs one of these, say so and suggest a local session on the Mac.
- **Health data stays out:** never pull DexaProject, `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES`,
  or any folder whose `CLAUDE.md` says "local only" into a cloud session.

## Layout rules

Full rules — grouping depth, the depth-2 discovery limit, and the gitignored-subtree
trap — live in project memory: `project_dev-layout-and-discovery.md`.

- ~50 projects carry a substantive `CLAUDE.md` (the rest are `@AGENTS.md` pointers). Read it before working in one.

## Handling care

- `DexaProject/` holds identifiable health data. It lives on Google Drive, not in
  `~/DEV`: `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/DexaProject`

  See `PERFORMANCE.md`.
  Never paste its contents into chat, an artifact, or an external service.

## Keeping this true

When a file moves or a new project starts, **update the router in the same
turn**. A stale pointer is worse than no pointer.

The counts above are approximate on purpose — they convey scale, not state, and
a `~` keeps ordinary growth from making this file wrong. Re-measure them only
when one is off by enough to change a decision. Counts last checked 2026-10-23.

Memory files named in these indexes (`project_*.md`, `user_*.md`) live in the
workspace's Tier A folder: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/`. They auto-load
only when cwd is the workspace root itself — from inside a sub-project, open them by path.

"""WR on the FBS baseline: targets per snap (count only), multi-season, rolling 4-game windows, no grade features.

Outcome: PFF offense grade per WR per game. WR rows and snaps: data/oline_pull*.json (all positions).
Targets: data/wr_<season>.json (premium passing target_player_id). A target links to a WR when the same id is a
WR grade row in the same game. Link rate is reported. Field role is unverified against the PFF docs.
Before = 2026 weeks 1-4 only. After = all seasons pooled. Test: 2026 weeks 5 and 7, non-Baylor.
"""
import os, json, glob, warnings
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNetCV, ElasticNet
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
W = os.environ.get("PFF_WORK_DIR", "data")
WEEKS = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}
FEAT = ["targets_per_snap", "snaps"]

def season_position_targets(s, g, tp):
    """2023 to 2026 path. Targets come from data/wr_targets_<s>.json, which stores each target's position.
    A WR-coded target (position ends in WR) links to any grade row in the same game, because about a third
    of WR-coded receivers are graded as TE or HB. Those rows join the WR pool with role "target_link".
    shortcut: a TE or HB grade counts as a WR for the games it is a WR-coded target; upgrade when receiver snaps load.
    """
    d = json.load(open(tp))
    t = pd.DataFrame(d["targets"])
    t["game_id"] = t["game_id"].astype(str); t["player_id"] = t["player_id"].astype(str)
    t = t[t["week"].isin(WEEKS) & t["position"].str.endswith("WR")]
    keep = t.groupby(["game_id", "player_id"], as_index=False)["n_targets"].sum()
    key = lambda df: pd.MultiIndex.from_frame(df[["game_id", "player_id"]])
    any_grade = key(keep).isin(key(g))
    wr_grade = key(keep).isin(key(g[g["position"] == "WR"]))
    link = {"season": s, "target_ids": len(keep), "linked_to_wr": int(any_grade.sum()),
            "linked_to_wr_grade": int(wr_grade.sum()), "source": "api_position"}
    keep = keep[any_grade]
    wr = g[(g["position"] == "WR") | key(g).isin(key(keep))].copy()
    wr["role"] = np.where(wr["position"] == "WR", "WR grade", "target_link")
    wr["season"] = s; wr["week"] = wr["week"].astype(int)
    wr["snaps"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["snaps"], errors="coerce"); wr["offense"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["offense"], errors="coerce")
    wr["baylor"] = wr["team_id"] == "118"
    wr = wr.merge(keep, on=["game_id", "player_id"], how="left")
    wr["n_targets"] = wr["n_targets"].fillna(0)
    wr["targets_per_snap"] = wr["n_targets"] / wr["snaps"].replace(0, np.nan)
    return wr, link

def season(s):
    gp = os.path.join(W, "oline_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"oline_pull_{s}.json")
    fp = os.path.join(W, "fbs_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"fbs_pull_{s}.json")
    wp = os.path.join(W, f"wr_{s}.json")
    if not all(os.path.exists(x) for x in [gp, fp, wp]):
        return None, None
    fbs = set(json.load(open(fp))["fbs_franchises"])
    g = pd.DataFrame(json.load(open(gp))["grades"])
    g["team_id"] = g["team_id"].astype(str); g["player_id"] = g["player_id"].astype(str)
    g = g[g["team_id"].isin(fbs)].drop_duplicates(["game_id", "player_id"])
    g = g[g["week"].isin(WEEKS)]
    tp = os.path.join(W, f"wr_targets_{s}.json")
    if os.path.exists(tp):
        return season_position_targets(s, g, tp)
    wr = g[g["position"] == "WR"].copy()
    wr["season"] = s; wr["week"] = wr["week"].astype(int)
    wr["snaps"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["snaps"], errors="coerce"); wr["offense"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["offense"], errors="coerce")
    wr["baylor"] = wr["team_id"] == "118"
    w = json.load(open(wp))
    tg = pd.DataFrame(w["targets"])
    tg["player_id"] = tg["player_id"].astype(str)
    # link check: each target id should be a WR grade row in the same game
    wr_keys = set(zip(wr["game_id"], wr["player_id"]))
    tg["is_wr"] = [ (gid, pid) in wr_keys for gid, pid in zip(tg["game_id"], tg["player_id"]) ]
    link = {"season": s, "target_ids": len(tg), "linked_to_wr": int(tg["is_wr"].sum()), "games": len(w["games"]),
            "games_with_target_field": int(sum(1 for x in w["games"] if x["rows_with_target"] > 0)),
            "passing_rows": int(sum(x["passing_rows"] for x in w["games"])), "rows_with_target": int(sum(x["rows_with_target"] for x in w["games"]))}
    tg = tg[tg["is_wr"]][["game_id", "player_id", "n_targets"]]
    wr = wr.merge(tg, on=["game_id", "player_id"], how="left")
    wr["n_targets"] = wr["n_targets"].fillna(0)
    wr["targets_per_snap"] = wr["n_targets"] / wr["snaps"].replace(0, np.nan)
    return wr, link

frames, links = [], []
for s in range(2018, 2027):
    f, l = season(s)
    if f is not None:
        frames.append(f); links.append(l)
pd.DataFrame(links).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_link_rates.csv"), index=False)
print(pd.DataFrame(links).to_string(index=False))
allw = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
allw = allw[(allw.snaps > 0) & allw.offense.notna()].dropna(subset=FEAT).copy()
print("WR player-games:", len(allw), "baylor:", int(allw.baylor.sum()), "players:", allw[~allw.baylor].player_id.nunique())
allw = allw.sort_values(["season", "player_id", "week"])
for col in FEAT + ["offense"]:
    allw[f"roll4_{col}"] = allw.groupby(["season", "player_id"])[col].transform(lambda s_: s_.rolling(4, min_periods=2).mean())
ROLLF = [f"roll4_{f}" for f in FEAT]
test_m = lambda d: (d.season == 2026) & d.week.isin([5, 7]) & (~d.baylor)
trn_m = lambda d: (~d.baylor) & ((d.season < 2026) | ((d.season == 2026) & (d.week <= 4)))

def fit_en(X, y, groups):
    return ElasticNetCV(l1_ratio=[0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0], alphas=np.logspace(-3, 1, 30),
                        cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=4).split(X, y, groups), max_iter=20000).fit(X, y)

def score(feats, target, label, pool):
    d = allw.dropna(subset=feats + [target]); tr = d[trn_m(d) & pool(d)]; te = d[test_m(d)]
    if len(tr) < 30 or len(te) < 5:
        print(label, "too few", len(tr), len(te)); return None
    mu, sd = tr[feats].mean(), tr[feats].std().replace(0, 1)
    Z = lambda x: ((x[feats] - mu) / sd).values
    en = fit_en(Z(tr), tr[target].values, tr.game_id.values)
    r2 = r2_score(te[target], en.predict(Z(te)))
    print(f"{label}: test R2={r2:.3f} train n={len(tr)} test n={len(te)}", flush=True)
    return r2, len(tr), len(te), en, mu, sd, Z, d

rows = []
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "BEFORE: 2026 weeks 1-4 only", lambda d: d.season == 2026)
if r: rows.append(("before: 2026 weeks 1-4, single-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "AFTER A: all seasons pooled, single-game", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r: rows.append(("after A: all seasons, single-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
r = score(ROLLF, "roll4_offense", "AFTER B: all seasons, rolling 4-game", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r: rows.append(("after B: all seasons, rolling 4-game", r[0], r[1], r[2]))
pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", "test_R2", "n_train", "n_test"]).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_results.csv"), index=False)
r = score(FEAT, "offense", "coefficients (pooled single-game)", lambda d: d.season > 0)
if r:
    _, _, _, en, mu, sd, Z, d = r
    tr_all = d[~d.baylor]; games = tr_all.game_id.unique(); rng = np.random.default_rng(11); B = []
    for _ in range(200):
        pk = rng.choice(games, len(games), replace=True)
        bs = pd.concat([tr_all[tr_all.game_id == gg] for gg in pk])
        B.append(ElasticNet(alpha=en.alpha_, l1_ratio=en.l1_ratio_, max_iter=20000).fit(((bs[FEAT] - mu) / sd).values, bs["offense"].values).coef_)
    B = np.array(B)
    for i, f in enumerate(FEAT):
        print(f"   {f:18s} coef={en.coef_[i]:+.3f} CI [{np.percentile(B[:, i], 2.5):+.3f}, {np.percentile(B[:, i], 97.5):+.3f}]")
    by = d[d.baylor].copy(); by["pred"] = en.predict(Z(by)); by["resid"] = by["offense"] - by["pred"]
    print(f"Baylor WR player-games n={len(by)}: mean residual={by.resid.mean():+.2f}")
    bg = by.game_id.unique(); bb = []
    for _ in range(1000):
        pk = rng.choice(bg, len(bg), replace=True); bb.append(by[by.game_id.isin(pk)].resid.mean())
    print(f"   bootstrap 95% CI [{np.percentile(bb, 2.5):+.2f}, {np.percentile(bb, 97.5):+.2f}]")
    by[["season", "week", "game_id", "team_id", "player_id", "snaps", "n_targets", "offense", "pred", "resid"]].round(3).to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_baylor_scored.csv"), index=False)
    allw[["season", "week", "game_id", "team_id", "player_id", "snaps", "n_targets", "targets_per_snap", "offense", "baylor"]].to_csv(os.path.join(W, "wr_player_game.csv"), index=False)

"""WR on the FBS baseline: targets per snap (count only), multi-season, rolling 4-game windows, no grade features.

Outcome: PFF offense grade per WR per game. WR rows and snaps: data/oline_pull*.json (all positions).
Targets: data/wr_<season>.json (premium passing target_player_id). A target links to a WR when the same id is a
WR grade row in the same game. Link rate is reported. Field role is unverified against the PFF docs.
Before = 2026 weeks 1-4 only. After = all seasons pooled. Test: 2026 weeks 5 and 7, non-Baylor.
"""
import os, json, glob, warnings
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNetCV, ElasticNet
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
W = os.environ.get("PFF_WORK_DIR", "data")
WEEKS = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}
FEAT = ["targets_per_snap", "snaps"]

def season_position_targets(s, g, tp):
    """2023 to 2026 path. Targets come from data/wr_targets_<s>.json, which stores each target's position.
    A WR-coded target (position ends in WR) links to a WR grade row in the same game. Rows graded as TE or HB
    are dropped from the outcome, so the WR pool is WR grades only (decision: Eric, 2026-10-23).
    """
    d = json.load(open(tp))
    t = pd.DataFrame(d["targets"])
    t["game_id"] = t["game_id"].astype(str); t["player_id"] = t["player_id"].astype(str)
    t = t[t["week"].isin(WEEKS) & t["position"].str.endswith("WR")]
    keep = t.groupby(["game_id", "player_id"], as_index=False)["n_targets"].sum()
    key = lambda df: pd.MultiIndex.from_frame(df[["game_id", "player_id"]])
    any_grade = key(keep).isin(key(g))
    wr_grade = key(keep).isin(key(g[g["position"] == "WR"]))
    link = {"season": s, "target_ids": len(keep), "linked_to_wr": int(any_grade.sum()),
            "linked_to_wr_grade": int(wr_grade.sum()), "source": "api_position"}
    keep = keep[any_grade]
    wr = g[(g["position"] == "WR") | key(g).isin(key(keep))].copy()
    wr["role"] = np.where(wr["position"] == "WR", "WR grade", "target_link")
    wr["season"] = s; wr["week"] = wr["week"].astype(int)
    wr["snaps"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["snaps"], errors="coerce"); wr["offense"] = pd.to_numeric(wr["offense"], errors="coerce")
    wr["baylor"] = wr["team_id"] == "118"
    wr = wr.merge(keep, on=["game_id", "player_id"], how="left")
    wr["n_targets"] = wr["n_targets"].fillna(0)
    wr["targets_per_snap"] = wr["n_targets"] / wr["snaps"].replace(0, np.nan)
    return wr, link

def season(s):
    gp = os.path.join(W, "oline_pull.json" if s == 2026 else f"oline_pull_{s}.json")

cd /Users/kristinarash/DEV/Football/PFF_Position_Reports && /Users/kristinarash/.local/share/pff-data/venv/bin/python -c "
import json, pandas as pd
W={1,2,3,4,5,7}
for s in [2023,2024,2025,2026]:
    gp='data/oline_pull.json' if s==2026 else f'data/oline_pull_{s}.json'
    fp='data/fbs_pull.json' if s==2026 else f'data/fbs_pull_{s}.json'
    fbs=set(json.load(open(fp))['fbs_franchises'])
    g=pd.DataFrame(json.load(open(gp))['grades']); g['team_id']=g.team_id.astype(str); g['player_id']=g.player_id.astype(str); g['game_id']=g.game_id.astype(str)
    g=g[g.team_id.isin(fbs)].drop_duplicates(['game_id','player_id']); g=g[g.week.isin(W)]
    t=pd.DataFrame(json.load(open(f'data/wr_targets_{s}.json'))['targets']); t['game_id']=t.game_id.astype(str); t['player_id']=t.player_id.astype(str)
    t=t[t.week.isin(W) & t.position.str.endswith('WR')]
    k=t.groupby(['game_id','player_id'],as_index=False).n_targets.sum()
    gk=g.set_index(['game_id','player_id']).position
    k['gpos']=[gk.get((a,b),None) for a,b in zip(k.game_id,k.player_id)]
    tot=int(k.n_targets.sum()); wr=int(k[k.gpos=='WR'].n_targets.sum())
    vc=k.groupby(k.gpos.fillna('no grade')).n_targets.agg(['size','sum']).to_dict('index')
    print(s,'WR-coded target pairs',len(k),'| targets',tot,'| kept (WR grade)',wr,f'({wr/tot:.1%})','| dropped',tot-wr, '| by grade pos', {p:(v['size'],int(v['sum'])) for p,v in vc.items() if p!='WR'})
"

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,

import json, pandas as pd
W={1,2,3,4,5,7}
for s in [2023,2024,2025,2026]:
    gp='data/oline_pull.json' if s==2026 else f'data/oline_pull_{s}.json'
    fp='data/fbs_pull.json' if s==2026 else f'data/fbs_pull_{s}.json'
    fbs=set(json.load(open(fp))['fbs_franchises'])
    g=pd.DataFrame(json.load(open(gp))['grades']); g['team_id']=g.team_id.astype(str); g['player_id']=g.player_id.astype(str); g['game_id']=g.game_id.astype(str)
    g=g[g.team_id.isin(fbs)].drop_duplicates(['game_id','player_id']); g=g[g.week.isin(W)]
    g['snaps']=pd.to_numeric(g.snaps,errors='coerce')
    t=pd.DataFrame(json.load(open(f'data/wr_targets_{s}.json'))['targets']); t['game_id']=t.game_id.astype(str); t['player_id']=t.player_id.astype(str)
    t=t[t.week.isin(W) & t.position.str.endswith('WR')]
    k=t.groupby(['game_id','player_id'],as_index=False).n_targets.sum()
    gi=g.set_index(['game_id','player_id'])
    k=k.join(gi[['position','snaps']], on=['game_id','player_id'])
    grp=k.position.fillna('no grade').map(lambda p: 'WR' if p=='WR' else ('TE_HB' if p in ('TE','HB') else ('no grade' if p=='no grade' else 'other')))
    n=len(k)
    c=k.assign(grp=grp).groupby('grp').agg(pairs=('n_targets','size'),targets=('n_targets','sum'))
    tot=k.n_targets.sum()
    # per-snap: full pool = linked rows with grade (any position), WR pool = WR-graded rows
    linked=k[k.position.notna()]
    full_ts=linked.n_targets.sum()/linked.snaps.sum()
    wrp=k[k.position=='WR']; wr_ts=wrp.n_targets.sum()/wrp.snaps.sum()
    print(s, 'pairs',n, {r:int(c.loc[r,'pairs']) if r in c.index else 0 for r in ['WR','TE_HB','other','no grade']}, '| targets',int(tot), {r:int(c.loc[r,'targets']) if r in c.index else 0 for r in ['WR','TE_HB','other','no grade']}, '| kept share of targets', round(c.loc['WR','targets']/tot*100,1) if 'WR' in c.index else None, '% | targets per snap full pool', round(full_ts,4), 'WR pool', round(wr_ts,4))
"
